functions.name: ClfsAddLogContainer
functions.summary: The ClfsAddLogContainer function adds a container to a CLFS log.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS ClfsAddLogContainer(PLOG_FILE_OBJECT plfoLog, PULONGLONG pcbContainer, PUNICODE_STRING puszContainerPath);

params.name: plfoLog
params.description: A pointer to a LOG_FILE_OBJECT structure that represents the log to which the container will be added. The caller previously obtained this pointer by calling ClfsCreateLogFile.

params.name: pcbContainer
params.description: A pointer to a ULONGLONG-typed variable. The role of this parameter depends on whether the log currently has at least one container.

params.name: puszContainerPath
params.description: A pointer to a UNICODE_STRING structure that supplies the path name for the new container. The path can be absolute or relative to the location of the base log file. Paths that are relative to the base log file must begin with CLFS_CONTAINER_RELATIVE_PREFIX, which is the string literal (L"%BLF%\\").

returns.description: ClfsAddLogContainer returns STATUS_SUCCESS if it succeeds; otherwise, it returns one of the error codes defined in Ntstatus.h.

functions.name: ClfsAddLogContainerSet
functions.summary: The ClfsAddLogContainerSet function atomically adds a set of containers to a CLFS log.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS ClfsAddLogContainerSet(PLOG_FILE_OBJECT plfoLog, USHORT cContainers, PULONGLONG pcbContainer, PUNICODE_STRING rguszContainerPath);

params.name: plfoLog
params.description: A pointer to a LOG_FILE_OBJECT structure that represents the log to which the containers will be added. The caller previously obtained this pointer by calling ClfsCreateLogFile.

params.name: cContainers
params.description: The number of containers in the set. This is the number of elements in the rguszContainerPath array.

params.name: pcbContainer
params.description: A pointer to a ULONGLONG-typed variable. The role of this parameter depends on whether the log currently has at least one container.

params.name: rguszContainerPath
params.description: A pointer to an array of UNICODE_STRING structures. Each string supplies the path name for one of the new containers. The number of elements in the array is given by cContainers. A given path can be absolute or relative to the location of the base log file. Paths that are relative to the base log file must begin with CLFS_CONTAINER_RELATIVE_PREFIX, which is the string literal (L"%BLF%\\").

returns.description: ClfsAddLogContainer returns STATUS_SUCCESS if it succeeds; otherwise, it returns one of the error codes defined in Ntstatus.h.

functions.name: ClfsAdvanceLogBase
functions.summary: The ClfsAdvanceLogBase function sets the base LSN of a CLFS stream.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS ClfsAdvanceLogBase(PVOID pvMarshalContext, PCLFS_LSN plsnBase, ULONG fFlags);

params.name: pvMarshalContext
params.description: A pointer to an opaque context that represents a marshalling area associated with a CLFS stream. The caller previously obtained this pointer by calling ClfsCreateMarshallingArea.

params.name: plsnBase
params.description: A pointer to a CLFS_LSN structure that contains the new base LSN. This parameter must be the LSN of one of the records in the stream. Also, this parameter must be greater than or equal to the stream's current base LSN and less than or equal to the stream's current last LSN.

params.name: fFlags
params.description: This parameter is reserved for system use. Callers must set this parameter to zero.

returns.description: ClfsAdvanceLogBase returns STATUS_SUCCESS if it succeeds; otherwise, it returns one of the error codes defined in Ntstatus.h.

functions.name: ClfsAlignReservedLog
functions.summary: The ClfsAlignReservedLog function calculates the size of the space that must be reserved for a specified set of records. The size calculation includes the space required for headers and the space required for sector alignment.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS ClfsAlignReservedLog(PVOID pvMarshalContext, ULONG cRecords, LONGLONG * rgcbReservation, PLONGLONG pcbAlignReservation);

params.name: pvMarshalContext
params.description: A pointer to an opaque context that represents a marshalling area associated with a CLFS stream. The caller previously obtained this pointer by calling ClfsCreateMarshallingArea.

params.name: cRecords
params.description: The number of elements in the array pointed to by rgcbReservation.

params.name: rgcbReservation
params.description: A pointer to an array of LONGLONG-typed variables that supplies a list of record sizes (in bytes).

params.name: pcbAlignReservation
params.description: A pointer to a LONGLONG-typed variable that receives the size, in bytes, of the required reservation.

returns.description: ClfsAlignReservedLog returns STATUS_SUCCESS if it succeeds; otherwise, it returns one of the error codes defined in Ntstatus.h.

functions.name: ClfsAllocReservedLog
functions.summary: The ClfsAllocReservedLog function reserves space in a marshalling area for a set of records.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS ClfsAllocReservedLog(PVOID pvMarshalContext, ULONG cRecords, PLONGLONG pcbAdjustment);

params.name: pvMarshalContext
params.description: A pointer to an opaque context that represents a marshalling area. The caller previously obtained this pointer by calling ClfsCreateMarshallingArea.

params.name: cRecords
params.description: The number of records in the set. This value must match the value of cRecords previously passed to ClfsAlignReservedLog.

params.name: pcbAdjustment
params.description: A pointer to a LONGLONG-typed variable that supplies the size, in bytes, of the reservation that will hold all the records in the set. The caller previously obtained this size by calling ClfsAlignReservedLog.

returns.description: ClfsAllocReservedLog returns STATUS_SUCCESS if it succeeds; otherwise, it returns one of the error codes defined in Ntstatus.h.

functions.name: ClfsCloseAndResetLogFile
functions.summary: The ClfsCloseAndResetLogFile function releases all references to a specified log file object and marks its associated stream for reset.

params.name: plfoLog
params.description: A pointer to a LOG_FILE_OBJECT structure for which references will be released. The caller previously obtained this pointer by calling ClfsCreateLogFile.

returns.description: ClfsCloseAndResetLogFile returns STATUS_SUCCESS if it succeeds; otherwise, it returns one of the error codes defined in Ntstatus.h.

functions.name: ClfsCloseLogFileObject
functions.summary: The ClfsCloseLogFileObject function releases all references to a log file object.

params.name: plfoLog
params.description: A pointer to the LOG_FILE_OBJECT structure for which references will be released.The caller previously obtained this pointer by calling ClfsCreateLogFile.

returns.description: ClfsCloseLogFileObject returns STATUS_SUCCESS if it succeeds; otherwise, it returns one of the error codes defined in Ntstatus.h.

functions.name: ClfsCreateLogFile
functions.summary: The ClfsCreateLogFile function creates or opens a CLFS stream. If necessary, ClfsCreateLogFile also creates the underlying physical log that holds the stream's records.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS ClfsCreateLogFile(PPLOG_FILE_OBJECT pplfoLog, PUNICODE_STRING puszLogFileName, ACCESS_MASK fDesiredAccess, ULONG dwShareMode, PSECURITY_DESCRIPTOR psdLogFile, ULONG fCreateDisposition, ULONG fCreateOptions, ULONG fFlagsAndAttributes, ULONG fLogOptionFlag, PVOID pvContext, ULONG cbContext);

params.name: pplfoLog
params.description: A pointer to a variable that receives a pointer to a LOG_FILE_OBJECT structure that represents an open instance of the stream.

params.name: puszLogFileName
params.description: A pointer to a UNICODE_STRING structure that supplies the name of the stream or the underlying physical log.

params.name: fDesiredAccess
params.description: An ACCESS_MASK that supplies the type of access the client will have (by using the pointer returned in pplfoLog) to the stream. If this parameter is zero, clients can query the stream for its attributes, but cannot read from or write to the stream. This parameter can be zero or any combination of the following flags:

params.name: dwShareMode
params.description: The sharing mode of the stream, which can be zero (not shared) or any combination of the following flags:

params.name: psdLogFile
params.description: A pointer to a SECURITY_DESCRIPTOR structure that supplies security attributes for the stream. This parameter can be NULL.

params.name: fCreateDisposition
params.description: The action to take that depends on whether the stream already exists. This parameter must be set to one of the following values:

params.name: fCreateOptions
params.description: A set of flags that specify options to apply when creating or opening the stream. This parameter can be zero or a compatible combination of the following flags:

params.name: fFlagsAndAttributes
params.description: A value that specifies whether the stream is opened for normal or read-only access. This parameter must be set to either

params.name: fLogOptionFlag
params.description: A hint about the relationship between CLFS and the component creating or opening the stream. This parameter must be set to one of the following values:

params.name: pvContext
params.description: A pointer to a context. The way the context is interpreted depends on the value passed to fLogOptionsFlag.

params.name: cbContext
params.description: The size, in bytes, of the context pointed to by pvContext. If pvContext is not NULL, this parameter must be greater than zero.

returns.description: ClfsCreateLogFile returns STATUS_SUCCESS if it succeeds; otherwise, it returns one of the error codes defined in Ntstatus.h.

functions.name: ClfsCreateMarshallingArea
functions.summary: The ClfsCreateMarshallingArea function creates a marshalling area for a CLFS stream and returns a pointer to an opaque context that represents the new marshalling area.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS ClfsCreateMarshallingArea(PLOG_FILE_OBJECT plfoLog, POOL_TYPE ePoolType, PALLOCATE_FUNCTION pfnAllocBuffer, PFREE_FUNCTION pfnFreeBuffer, ULONG cbMarshallingBuffer, ULONG cMaxWriteBuffers, ULONG cMaxReadBuffers, PVOID * ppvMarshalContext);

params.name: plfoLog
params.description: A pointer to a LOG_FILE_OBJECT structure that represents a CLFS stream. The caller previously obtained this pointer by calling ClfsCreateLogFile.

params.name: ePoolType
params.description: A POOL_TYPE value that specifies the type of memory (paged, non-paged, for example) that the new marshalling area will use for its log I/O blocks.

params.name: pfnAllocBuffer
params.description: Either NULL or a pointer to a caller-supplied function that allocates a log I/O block for the marshalling area. The allocation function has the following prototype:

params.name: pfnFreeBuffer
params.description: Either NULL or a pointer to a caller-supplied function that frees a log I/O block that was previously allocated by *pfnAllocBuffer*. The function has the following prototype:

params.name: cbMarshallingBuffer
params.description: The size, in bytes, of the individual log I/O blocks that the new marshalling area uses. This must be a multiple of the sector size on the stable storage medium. The sector size is the *lpBytesPerSector* value returned from GetDiskFreeSpace.

params.name: cMaxWriteBuffers
params.description: The maximum number of I/O blocks that can be allocated at one time for write operations. This parameter affects the frequency of data flushes. If you do not need to control the frequency of data flushes, set this parameter to INFINITE.

params.name: cMaxReadBuffers
params.description: The maximum number of log I/O blocks that can be allocated at one time for read operations.

params.name: ppvMarshalContext
params.description: A pointer to a variable that receives a pointer to an opaque context that represents the new marshalling area.

returns.description: ClfsCreateMarshallingArea returns STATUS_SUCCESS if it succeeds; otherwise, it returns one of the error codes defined in Ntstatus.h.

functions.name: ClfsCreateMarshallingAreaEx
functions.summary: Initializes a marshalling area for a physical or client log file stream.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS ClfsCreateMarshallingAreaEx(PLOG_FILE_OBJECT plfoLog, POOL_TYPE ePoolType, PALLOCATE_FUNCTION pfnAllocBuffer, PFREE_FUNCTION pfnFreeBuffer, ULONG cbMarshallingBuffer, ULONG cMaxWriteBuffers, ULONG cMaxReadBuffers, ULONG cAlignmentSize, ULONGLONG fFlags, PVOID * ppvMarshalContext);

params.name: plfoLog
params.description: The handle associated with new marshalling area.

params.name: ePoolType
params.description: Paged or non-paged pool buffers.

params.name: pfnAllocBuffer
params.description: Optional. A pointer to the block allocation callback function.

params.name: pfnFreeBuffer
params.description: Optional. A pointer to the block deallocation callback function.

params.name: cbMarshallingBuffer
params.description: The size of marshalling buffers.

params.name: cMaxWriteBuffers
params.description: The maximum number of allocated write buffers.

params.name: cMaxReadBuffers
params.description: The maximum number of allocated read buffers.

params.name: cAlignmentSize
params.description: The alignment size of marshalling buffers.

params.name: fFlags
params.description: buffer management flag

params.name: ppvMarshalContext
params.description: marshalling context

returns.description: This function returns CLFSUSER_API NTSTATUS.

functions.name: ClfsCreateScanContext
functions.summary: The ClfsCreateScanContext function creates a scan context that can be used to iterate over the containers of a specified CLFS log.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS ClfsCreateScanContext(PLOG_FILE_OBJECT plfoLog, ULONG cFromContainer, ULONG cContainers, CLFS_SCAN_MODE eScanMode, PCLFS_SCAN_CONTEXT pcxScan);

params.name: plfoLog
params.description: A pointer to a LOG_FILE_OBJECT structure that represents a CLFS stream. The scan context is created for the log that provides the underlying storage for that stream. The caller previously obtained this pointer by calling ClfsCreateLogFile.

params.name: cFromContainer
params.description: The index of the first container to be scanned. Containers are indexed starting at zero.

params.name: cContainers
params.description: The number of containers to be scanned with each call to ClfsScanLogContainers.

params.name: eScanMode
params.description: A set of flags that specify whether the scan context is set up for scanning forward or backward and whether the scan context should be reinitialized. The following three flags are available for callers of this function.

params.name: pcxScan
params.description: A pointer to a caller-allocated CLFS_SCAN_CONTEXT structure whose members are initialized by this function. This structure is later passed to ClfsScanLogContainers.

returns.description: ClfsCreateScanContext returns STATUS_SUCCESS if it succeeds; otherwise, it returns one of the error codes in Ntstatus.h.

functions.name: ClfsDeleteLogByPointer
functions.summary: The ClfsDeleteLogByPointer function marks a CLFS stream for deletion.

params.name: plfoLog
params.description: A pointer to a LOG_FILE_OBJECT structure that represents an open instance of the stream to be deleted. The caller previously obtained this pointer by calling ClfsCreateLogFile.

returns.description: ClfsDeleteLogByPointer returns STATUS_SUCCESS if it succeeds; otherwise, it returns one of the error codes defined in Ntstatus.h.

functions.name: ClfsDeleteLogFile
functions.summary: The ClfsDeleteLogFile function marks a CLFS stream for deletion.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS ClfsDeleteLogFile(PUNICODE_STRING puszLogFileName, PVOID pvReserved, ULONG fLogOptionFlag, PVOID pvContext, ULONG cbContext);

params.name: puszLogFileName
params.description: A pointer to a UNICODE_STRING structure that supplies the name of the CLFS stream to be deleted.

params.name: pvReserved
params.description: Reserved.

params.name: fLogOptionFlag
params.description: A value that indicates the relationship between CLFS and the component that is deleting the log. For a list of possible values, see the description of the fLogOptionFlag parameter of the ClfsCreateLogFile function.

params.name: pvContext
params.description: A pointer to a context. The way the context is interpreted depends on the value passed in fLogOptionFlag.

params.name: cbContext
params.description: The size, in bytes, of the context pointed to by pvContext. If pvContext is not NULL, this parameter must be greater than zero.

returns.description: ClfsDeleteLogFile returns STATUS_SUCCESS if it succeeds; otherwise, it returns one of the error codes defined in Ntstatus.h.

functions.name: ClfsDeleteMarshallingArea
functions.summary: The ClfsDeleteMarshallingArea function deletes a marshalling area.

params.name: pvMarshalContext
params.description: A pointer to an opaque context that represents a marshalling area. The caller previously obtained this pointer by calling ClfsCreateMarshallingArea.

returns.description: ClfsDeleteMarshallingArea returns STATUS_SUCCESS if it succeeds; otherwise, it returns one of the error codes defined in Ntstatus.h.

functions.name: ClfsFlushBuffers
functions.summary: The ClfsFlushBuffers function forces all log I/O blocks in a specified marshalling area to stable storage.

params.name: pvMarshalContext
params.description: A pointer to an opaque context that represents a marshalling area. The caller previously obtained this pointer by calling ClfsCreateMarshallingArea.

returns.description: ClfsFlushBuffers returns STATUS_SUCCESS if it succeeds; otherwise, it returns one of the error codes defined in Ntstatus.h.

functions.name: ClfsFlushToLsn
functions.summary: The ClfsFlushToLsn function forces, to stable storage, all records that have an LSN less than or equal to a specified LSN.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS ClfsFlushToLsn(PVOID pvMarshalContext, PCLFS_LSN plsnFlush, PCLFS_LSN plsnLastFlushed);

params.name: pvMarshalContext
params.description: A pointer to an opaque context associated with a marshalling area. The caller previously obtained this pointer by calling ClfsCreateMarshallingArea.

params.name: plsnFlush
params.description: A pointer to a CLFS_LSN structure. All records that have an LSN less than or equal to *plsnFlush* are guaranteed to be forced to stable storage. If *plsnFlush* is equal to CLFS_LSN_NULL, then all records in the marshalling area are forced to stable storage.

params.name: plsnLastFlushed
params.description: A pointer to a CLFS_LSN structure that receives the LSN of the oldest record that was not flushed. This is the LSN of the record immediately following the last record flushed.

returns.description: ClfsFlushToLsn returns STATUS_SUCCESS if it succeeds; otherwise, it returns one of the error codes defined in Ntstatus.h.

functions.name: ClfsGetContainerName
functions.summary: The ClfsGetContainerName function returns the path name of a specified container.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS ClfsGetContainerName(PLOG_FILE_OBJECT plfoLog, CLFS_CONTAINER_ID cidLogicalContainer, PUNICODE_STRING puszContainerName, PULONG pcActualLenContainerName);

params.name: plfoLog
params.description: A pointer to a LOG_FILE_OBJECT structure that represents a CLFS log. The caller previously obtained this pointer by calling ClfsCreateLogFile.

params.name: cidLogicalContainer
params.description: The logical identifier of a container in the CLFS log.

params.name: puszContainerName
params.description: A pointer to a UNICODE_STRING structure. The Buffer member of puszContainerName must point to a caller-allocated buffer that receives the path name of the container. The MaximumLength member must supply the size of the buffer.

params.name: pcActualLenContainerName
params.description: A pointer to a ULONG-typed variable that receives the actual length, in Unicode characters, of the container's path name. This parameter can be NULL.

returns.description: ClfsGetContainerName returns one of the status codes defined in Ntstatus.h. The following table gives the meanings of various return values.

functions.name: ClfsGetIoStatistics
functions.summary: The ClfsGetIoStatistics function returns I/O statistics for a specified CLFS log.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS ClfsGetIoStatistics(PLOG_FILE_OBJECT plfoLog, PVOID pvStatsBuffer, ULONG cbStatsBuffer, CLFS_IOSTATS_CLASS eStatsClass, PULONG pcbStatsWritten);

params.name: plfoLog
params.description: A pointer to a LOG_FILE_OBJECT structure that represents a CLFS stream. The I/O statistics will be collected for the stream's underlying log on stable storage. The caller previously obtained this pointer by calling ClfsCreateLogFile.

params.name: pvStatsBuffer
params.description: A pointer to a CLFS_IO_STATISTICS structure that receives the I/O statistics data.

params.name: cbStatsBuffer
params.description: The size, in bytes, of the buffer pointed to by pvStatsBuffer. This parameter must be at least sizeof(CLFS_IO_STATISTICS_HEADER). If this parameter is less than sizeof(CLFS_IO_STATISTICS), pvStatsBuffer will receive only a portion of the available I/O statistics.

params.name: eStatsClass
params.description: This parameter is reserved for future use.

params.name: pcbStatsWritten
params.description: A pointer to a ULONG-typed variable that receives the number of bytes actually written to pvStatsBuffer. This parameter can be NULL.

returns.description: ClfsGetIoStatistics returns STATUS_SUCCESS if it succeeds; otherwise, it returns one of the error codes defined in Ntstatus.h.

functions.name: ClfsLsnBlockOffset
functions.summary: The ClfsLsnBlockOffset function returns the sector-aligned block offset contained in a specified LSN.

params.name: plsn

functions.name: ClfsLsnContainer
functions.summary: The ClfsLsnContainer function returns the logical container identifier contained in a specified LSN.

params.description: A pointer to a CLFS_LSN structure from which the container identifier is retrieved.

returns.description: ClfsLsnContainer returns the logical container identifier contained in the LSN that is supplied by the caller. The logical container identifier is not necessarily the same as the identifier of the physical container on stable storage.

functions.name: ClfsLsnCreate
functions.summary: The ClfsLsnCreate function creates a log sequence number (LSN), given a container identifier, a block offset, and a record sequence number.

returns.description: ClfsLsnGreater returns TRUE if plsn1 is strictly greater than plsn2; otherwise, it returns FALSE.

functions.name: ClfsLsnLess

params.description: A pointer to a CLFS_LSN structure that supplies one of the LSNs to be compared.

params.name: plsn2
params.description: A pointer to a CLFS_LSN structure that supplies the other LSN to be compared.

returns.description: ClfsLsnLess returns TRUE if plsn1 is strictly less than plsn2; otherwise, it returns FALSE.

functions.name: ClfsLsnNull

returns.description: ClfsLsnNull returns TRUE if the LSN supplied by the caller is equal to CLFS_LSN_NULL; otherwise, it returns FALSE.

functions.name: ClfsLsnRecordSequence
functions.summary: The ClfsLsnRecordSequence function returns the record sequence number contained in a specified LSN.

params.name: plsn
params.description: A pointer to a CLFS_LSN structure from which the record sequence number is retrieved.

returns.description: ClfsLsnRecordSequence returns the record sequence number contained in the LSN that is supplied by the caller.

functions.signature: NTSTATUS ClfsMgmtQueryPolicy(PLOG_FILE_OBJECT LogFile, CLFS_MGMT_POLICY_TYPE PolicyType, PCLFS_MGMT_POLICY Policy, PULONG PolicyLength);

params.name: LogFile
params.description: A pointer to a LOG_FILE_OBJECT structure that represents the CLFS log whose policy is being retrieved.

params.name: PolicyType
params.description: A value of the CLFS_MGMT_POLICY_TYPE enumeration that identifies the type of policy to be retrieved.

params.name: Policy
params.description: An instance of the CLFS_MGMT_POLICY structure that contains the policy.

params.name: PolicyLength
params.description: The length of the Policy parameter.

returns.description: The ClfsMgmtQueryPolicy function returns one of the following NTSTATUS values:

functions.name: ClfsMgmtRegisterManagedClient
functions.summary: The ClfsMgmtRegisterManagedClient function creates a client that will manage a CLFS log.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS ClfsMgmtRegisterManagedClient(PLOG_FILE_OBJECT LogFile, PCLFS_MGMT_CLIENT_REGISTRATION RegistrationData, PCLFS_MGMT_CLIENT ClientCookie);

params.name: LogFile
params.description: A pointer to a LOG_FILE_OBJECT structure that represents the CLFS log stream that the client created by ClfsMgmtRegisterManagedClient will manage.

params.name: RegistrationData
params.description: An instance of the CLFS_MGMT_CLIENT_REGISTRATION structure that contains the functions that will be used to manage the log.

params.name: ClientCookie
params.description: The cookie we give back to the caller for future use of the API.

returns.description: The ClfsMgmtRegisterManagedClient function returns one of the following NTSTATUS values:

functions.name: ClfsMgmtRemovePolicy
functions.summary: The ClfsMgmtRemovePolicy function resets a log's CLFS_MGMT_POLICY structure to its default value.

params.name: LogFile
params.description: A pointer to a LOG_FILE_OBJECT structure that represents the CLFS log whose policy is being removed.

params.name: PolicyType
params.description: A value of the CLFS_MGMT_POLICY_TYPE enumeration that supplies the type of the policy to be removed.

returns.description: The ClfsMgmtRemovePolicy function returns one of the following NTSTATUS values:

functions.name: ClfsMgmtSetLogFileSize
functions.summary: The ClfsMgmtSetLogFileSize function adds containers to a log or deletes containers from a log.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS ClfsMgmtSetLogFileSize(PLOG_FILE_OBJECT LogFile, PULONGLONG NewSizeInContainers, PULONGLONG ResultingSizeInContainers, PCLFS_SET_LOG_SIZE_COMPLETE_CALLBACK CompletionRoutine, PVOID CompletionRoutineData);

params.name: LogFile
params.description: A pointer to a LOG_FILE_OBJECT structure that represents the CLFS log, or a stream within the log, to which containers are being added or deleted.

params.name: NewSizeInContainers
params.description: A pointer to the requested log size. The caller sets this parameter to one of the following values.

params.name: ResultingSizeInContainers
params.description: A pointer to the resulting log size. If successful, the function writes the actual size of the log, expressed as the number of containers in the log, to the location pointed to by this parameter.

params.name: CompletionRoutine
params.description: Not used. Set to NULL.

params.name: CompletionRoutineData
params.description: Not used. Set to NULL.

returns.description: The ClfsMgmtSetLogFileSize function returns one of the following NTSTATUS values:

functions.name: ClfsMgmtSetLogFileSizeAsClient
functions.summary: The ClfsMgmtSetLogFileSizeAsClient function sets the log file size by adding containers to a client log or deleting containers from a client log.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS ClfsMgmtSetLogFileSizeAsClient(PLOG_FILE_OBJECT LogFile, CLFS_MGMT_CLIENT ClientCookie, PULONGLONG NewSizeInContainers, PULONGLONG ResultingSizeInContainers, PCLFS_SET_LOG_SIZE_COMPLETE_CALLBACK CompletionRoutine, PVOID CompletionRoutineData);

params.name: LogFile
params.description: A pointer to a LOG_FILE_OBJECT structure that represents the Common Log File System (CLFS) log, or a stream within the log, to which containers are being added or deleted. The value of this parameter is obtained through a call to the ClfsCreateLogFile function.

params.name: ClientCookie
params.description: A pointer to a client-supplied cookie. The value of this parameter should be the CLFS_MGMT_CLIENT structure that is obtained through a call to the ClfsMgmtRegisterManagedClient function.

params.name: NewSizeInContainers
params.description: The desired size of the log, expressed in the number of containers. There can be at most 1,024 containers for a log file.

params.name: ResultingSizeInContainers
params.description: The actual size of the log, expressed in the number of containers.

params.name: CompletionRoutine
params.description: Not used.

params.name: CompletionRoutineData
params.description: Not used.

returns.description: The ClfsMgmtSetLogFileSizeAsClient function returns an NTSTATUS value.

functions.name: ClfsMgmtTailAdvanceFailure
functions.summary: The ClfsMgmtTailAdvanceFailure function notifies CLFS management that the client could not advance the log's tail.

params.name: Client
params.description: A pointer to the client. This is the value that was obtained through a call to the ClfsMgmtRegisterManagedClient function.

params.name: Reason
params.description: A value that indicates why the log's tail could not be advanced.

returns.description: The ClfsMgmtTailAdvanceFailure function returns one of the following NTSTATUS values:

functions.name: ClfsQueryLogFileInformation
functions.summary: The ClfsQueryLogFileInformation function returns metadata and state information for a specified CLFS stream or its underlying physical log or both.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS ClfsQueryLogFileInformation(PLOG_FILE_OBJECT plfoLog, CLFS_LOG_INFORMATION_CLASS eInformationClass, PVOID pinfoInputBuffer, ULONG cbinfoInputBuffer, PVOID pinfoBuffer, PULONG pcbInfoBuffer);

params.name: plfoLog
params.description: A pointer to a LOG_FILE_OBJECT structure that represents a CLFS stream. The caller previously obtained this pointer by calling ClfsCreateLogFile.

params.name: eInformationClass
params.description: A value from the CLFS_LOG_INFORMATION_CLASS enumeration that specifies the type of information being requested.

params.name: pinfoInputBuffer
params.description: Optional input buffer which is required for some information classes.

params.name: cbinfoInputBuffer
params.description: Length in bytes of pinfoInputBuffer.

params.name: pinfoBuffer
params.description: A pointer to a buffer that receives the log information. The structure of this buffer depends on the value of eInformationClass. The following table shows the relationship between the information class and the data type of the buffer.

params.name: pcbInfoBuffer
params.description: Length in bytes of the incoming information buffer.

returns.description: ClfsQueryLogFileInformation returns STATUS_SUCCESS if it succeeds; otherwise, it returns one of the error codes defined in Ntstatus.h.

functions.name: ClfsReadLogRecord
functions.summary: The ClfsReadLogRecord function reads a target record in a CLFS stream and returns a read context that the caller can use to read the records preceding or following it in the stream.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS ClfsReadLogRecord(PVOID pvMarshalContext, PCLFS_LSN plsnFirst, CLFS_CONTEXT_MODE peContextMode, PVOID * ppvReadBuffer, PULONG pcbReadBuffer, PCLFS_RECORD_TYPE peRecordType, PCLFS_LSN plsnUndoNext, PCLFS_LSN plsnPrevious, PVOID * ppvReadContext);

params.name: pvMarshalContext
params.description: A pointer to an opaque context that represents a marshalling area. The caller previously obtained this pointer by calling ClfsCreateMarshallingArea.

params.name: plsnFirst
params.description: A pointer to a CLFS_LSN structure that supplies the LSN of the target record in the log.

params.name: peContextMode
params.description: A value from the CLFS_CONTEXT_MODE enumeration that specifies the initial mode (ClfsContextUndoNext, ClfsContextPrevious, or ClfsContextForward) of the read context returned in ppvReadContext.

params.name: ppvReadBuffer
params.description: A pointer to a variable that receives a pointer to the data buffer of the target record.

params.name: pcbReadBuffer
params.description: A pointer to a ULONG-typed variable that receives the size, in bytes, of the buffer pointed to by ppvReadBuffer*. This is the length of the data buffer of the target record.

params.name: peRecordType
params.description: A pointer to a variable of type CLFS_RECORD_TYPE that receives one of the following values.

params.name: plsnUndoNext
params.description: A pointer to a CLFS_LSN structure that receives the undo-next LSN of the target record.

params.name: plsnPrevious
params.description: A pointer to a CLFS_LSN structure that receives the previous LSN of the target record.

params.name: ppvReadContext
params.description: A pointer to a variable that receives a pointer to an opaque read context. The client repeatedly passes this context to ClfsReadNextLogRecord to read the remaining records in a sequence. After the client has read all the records in the sequence, it calls ClfsTerminateReadLog to free the read context.

returns.description: ClfsReadLogRecord returns STATUS_SUCCESS if it succeeds; otherwise, it returns one of the error codes defined in Ntstatus.h.

functions.name: ClfsReadNextLogRecord
functions.summary: The ClfsReadNextLogRecord function reads the next record in a sequence, relative to the current record in a read context.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS ClfsReadNextLogRecord(PVOID pvReadContext, PVOID * ppvBuffer, PULONG pcbBuffer, PCLFS_RECORD_TYPE peRecordType, PCLFS_LSN plsnUser, PCLFS_LSN plsnUndoNext, PCLFS_LSN plsnPrevious, PCLFS_LSN plsnRecord);

params.name: pvReadContext
params.description: A pointer to a read context that the caller previously obtained by calling ClfsReadLogRecord or ClfsReadRestartArea.

params.name: ppvBuffer
params.description: A pointer to a variable that receives a pointer to a buffer that contains the record data.

params.name: pcbBuffer
params.description: A pointer to a ULONG-typed variable that receives the size, in bytes, of the buffer pointed to by ppvBuffer*. This is the length of the data buffer of the record read.

params.name: peRecordType
params.description: A pointer to a variable of type CLFS_RECORD_TYPE. The caller must set this parameter to one of the following values.

params.name: plsnUser
params.description: A pointer to a CLFS_LSN structure that supplies the LSN of the record to be read. The specified record is read instead of the record that would have been read according to the mode (ClfsContextUndoNext, ClfsContextPrevious, or ClfsContextForward) of the read context (pvReadContext). The LSN supplied in plsnUser must be less than the current LSN of the read context. This parameter can be NULL.

params.name: plsnUndoNext
params.description: A pointer to a CLFS_LSN structure that receives the undo-next LSN of the record that is read.

params.name: plsnPrevious
params.description: A pointer to a CLFS_LSN structure that receives the previous LSN of the record that was read.

params.name: plsnRecord
params.description: A pointer to a CLFS_LSN structure that receives the LSN of the record that was read.

returns.description: ClfsReadNextLogRecord returns STATUS_SUCCESS if it succeeds; otherwise, it returns one of the error codes defined in Ntstatus.h.

functions.name: ClfsReadPreviousRestartArea
functions.summary: The ClfsReadPreviousRestartArea function reads the previous restart record relative to the current record in a read context.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS ClfsReadPreviousRestartArea(PVOID pvReadContext, PVOID * ppvRestartBuffer, PULONG pcbRestartBuffer, PCLFS_LSN plsnRestart);

params.name: pvReadContext
params.description: A pointer to a read context obtained by a previous call to ClfsReadRestartArea.

params.name: ppvRestartBuffer
params.description: A pointer to a variable that receives a pointer to the data buffer of the restart record that is read.

params.name: pcbRestartBuffer
params.description: A pointer to a ULONG-typed variable that receives the size, in bytes, of the buffer pointed to by ppvRestartBuffer*. This is the length of the data buffer of the restart record that is read.

params.name: plsnRestart
params.description: A pointer to a CLFS_LSN structure that receives the previous LSN of the restart record that was read.

returns.description: ClfsReadPreviousRestartArea returns STATUS_SUCCESS if it succeeds; otherwise, it returns one of the error codes defined in Ntstatus.h. If there are no previous restart areas, the return value is STATUS_LOG_START_OF_LOG.

functions.name: ClfsReadRestartArea
functions.summary: The ClfsReadRestartArea function reads the restart record that was most recently written to a specified CLFS stream.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS ClfsReadRestartArea(PVOID pvMarshalContext, PVOID * ppvRestartBuffer, PULONG pcbRestartBuffer, PCLFS_LSN plsn, PVOID * ppvReadContext);

params.name: pvMarshalContext
params.description: A pointer to an opaque context that represents a marshalling area associated with a CLFS stream. The caller previously obtained this pointer by calling ClfsCreateMarshallingArea.

params.name: ppvRestartBuffer
params.description: A pointer to a variable that receives a pointer to the data buffer of the restart record.

params.name: pcbRestartBuffer
params.description: A pointer to a ULONG-typed variable that receives the size, in bytes, of the data buffer pointed to by pcbRestartBuffer. This is the length of the data buffer of the restart record.

params.name: plsn
params.description: A pointer to a CLFS_LSN structure that receives the LSN of the restart record that was read.

params.name: ppvReadContext
params.description: A pointer to a variable that receives a pointer to an opaque read context. The caller can pass this context to ClfsReadPreviousRestartArea or ClfsReadNextLogRecord. When the caller has finished using the read context, it must free the context by calling ClfsTerminateReadLog.

returns.description: ClfsReadRestartArea returns STATUS_SUCCESS if it succeeds; otherwise, it returns one of the error codes defined in Ntstatus.h.

functions.name: ClfsRemoveLogContainer
functions.summary: The ClfsRemoveLogContainer function removes a container from a CLFS log.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS ClfsRemoveLogContainer(PLOG_FILE_OBJECT plfoLog, PUNICODE_STRING puszContainerPath, BOOLEAN fForce);

params.name: plfoLog
params.description: A pointer to a LOG_FILE_OBJECT structure that represents a CLFS log from which the container will be removed. The caller previously obtained this pointer by calling ClfsCreateLogFile.

params.name: puszContainerPath
params.description: A pointer to a UNICODE_STRING structure that supplies the path name for the container to be removed. The path name was created in a previous call to ClfsAddLogContainer or ClfsAddLogContainerSet. The path can be absolute or relative to the location of the base log file for the CLFS log that is represented by plfoLog. Paths that are relative to the base log file must begin with CLFS_CONTAINER_RELATIVE_PREFIX, which is the string literal (L"%BLF%\\"). The directories "." and ".." are not allowed in a relative path.

params.name: fForce
params.description: A Boolean value that specifies whether the container removal is forced (TRUE) or lazy (FALSE).

returns.description: ClfsRemoveLogContainer returns STATUS_SUCCESS if it succeeds; otherwise, it returns one of the error codes defined in Ntstatus.h.

functions.name: ClfsRemoveLogContainerSet
functions.summary: The ClfsRemoveLogContainerSet function atomically removes a set of containers from a CLFS log.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS ClfsRemoveLogContainerSet(PLOG_FILE_OBJECT plfoLog, USHORT cContainers, PUNICODE_STRING rgwszContainerPath, BOOLEAN fForce);

params.name: plfoLog
params.description: A pointer to a LOG_FILE_OBJECT structure that represents the CLFS log from which the containers will be removed. The caller previously obtained this pointer by calling ClfsCreateLogFile.

params.name: cContainers
params.description: The number of containers in the set. This is the number of elements in the rgwszContainerPath array.

params.name: rgwszContainerPath
params.description: A pointer to an array of UNICODE_STRING structures, each of which supplies the path name for one of the containers to be removed. The number of elements in the array is given by cContainers. A given path can be absolute or relative to the location of the base log file for the CLFS log represented by plfoLog. Paths that are relative to the base log file must begin with CLFS_CONTAINER_RELATIVE_PREFIX, which is the string literal (L"%BLF%\\"). The directories "." and ".." are not allowed in a relative path.

params.name: fForce
params.description: A Boolean value that specifies whether the container removal is forced (TRUE) or lazy (FALSE).

returns.description: ClfsRemoveLogContainerSet returns STATUS_SUCCESS if it succeeds; otherwise, it returns one of the error codes defined in Ntstatus.h.

functions.name: ClfsReserveAndAppendLog
functions.summary: The ClfsReserveAndAppendLog function reserves space in a marshalling area or appends a record to a marshalling area or does both atomically.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS ClfsReserveAndAppendLog(PVOID pvMarshalContext, PCLFS_WRITE_ENTRY rgWriteEntries, ULONG cWriteEntries, PCLFS_LSN plsnUndoNext, PCLFS_LSN plsnPrevious, ULONG cReserveRecords, PLONGLONG rgcbReservation, ULONG fFlags, PCLFS_LSN plsn);

params.name: pvMarshalContext
params.description: A pointer to an opaque context that represents a marshalling area associated with a CLFS stream. The caller previously obtained this pointer by calling ClfsCreateMarshallingArea.

params.name: rgWriteEntries
params.description: A pointer to an array of CLFS_WRITE_ENTRY structures, each of which holds a pointer to a buffer of data that will become part of the record that is appended to the log. This parameter can be NULL if cWriteEntries is zero.

params.name: cWriteEntries
params.description: The number of elements in the array pointed to by rgWriteEntries. This parameter must be zero if rgWriteEntries is NULL.

params.name: plsnUndoNext
params.description: A pointer to a CLFS_LSN structure that supplies the undo-next LSN of the record to be appended.

params.name: plsnPrevious
params.description: A pointer to a CLFS_LSN structure that supplies the previous LSN of the record to be appended.

params.name: cReserveRecords
params.description: The number of elements in the array pointed to by rgcbReservation. This parameter must be zero if rgcbReservation is NULL or the CLFS_FLAG_USE_RESERVATION flag of fFlags is set.

params.name: rgcbReservation
params.description: A pointer to an array of LONGLONG-typed variables. The caller sets each element of the array to the size, in bytes, of a record that must have space reserved for it. On return, each array element receives that actual size of the space reserved for the record. This includes the space required for headers and alignment. If the reservation value is negative, a reserved record that most nearly matches the absolute value of the provided negative value will be freed. This parameter can be NULL if cReserveRecords is zero and must be NULL if the CLFS_FLAG_USE_RESERVATION flag of fFlags is set.

params.name: fFlags
params.description: This parameter can be zero or any combination of the following flags.

params.name: plsn
params.description: A pointer to a CLFS_LSN structure that receives the LSN of the appended record. This parameter can be NULL if cWriteEntries is zero.

returns.description: ClfsReserveAndAppendLog returns STATUS_SUCCESS if it succeeds; otherwise, it returns one of the error codes defined in Ntstatus.h.

functions.name: ClfsReserveAndAppendLogAligned
functions.summary: The ClfsReserveAndAppendLogAligned function reserves space in a marshalling area or appends a record to a marshalling area or does both atomically. The record's data is aligned on specified boundaries.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS ClfsReserveAndAppendLogAligned(PVOID pvMarshalContext, PCLFS_WRITE_ENTRY rgWriteEntries, ULONG cWriteEntries, ULONG cbEntryAlignment, PCLFS_LSN plsnUndoNext, PCLFS_LSN plsnPrevious, ULONG cReserveRecords, PLONGLONG rgcbReservation, ULONG fFlags, PCLFS_LSN plsn);

params.name: pvMarshalContext
params.description: A pointer to an opaque context that represents a marshalling area associated with a CLFS stream. The caller previously obtained this pointer by calling ClfsCreateMarshallingArea.

params.name: rgWriteEntries
params.description: A pointer to an array of CLFS_WRITE_ENTRY structures, each of which holds a pointer to a buffer of data that will become part of the record that is appended to the log. This parameter can be NULL if cWriteEntries is zero.

params.name: cWriteEntries
params.description: The number of elements in the array pointed to by rgWriteEntries. This parameter must be zero if rgWriteEntries is NULL.

params.name: cbEntryAlignment
params.description: The byte alignment of the data entries pointed to by rgWriteEntries as they are marshaled into a single record. A value of one specifies simple concatenation (see ClfsReserveAndAppendLog). A value larger than one can result in zeros being placed between entries in the record. The value of this parameter must be greater than zero.

params.name: plsnUndoNext
params.description: A pointer to a CLFS_LSN structure that supplies the undo-next LSN of the record to be appended.

params.name: plsnPrevious
params.description: A pointer to a CLFS_LSN structure that supplies the previous LSN of the record to be appended.

params.name: cReserveRecords
params.description: The number of elements in the array pointed to by rgcbReservation. This parameter must be zero if rgcbReservation is NULL or the CLFS_FLAG_USE_RESERVATION flag of fFlags is set.

params.name: rgcbReservation
params.description: A pointer to an array of LONGLONG-typed variables. The caller sets each element of the array to the size, in bytes, of a record that must have space reserve for it. On return, each array element receives that actual size of the space reserved for the record. This includes the space required for headers and alignment. If the reservation value is negative, a reserved record that most nearly matches the absolute value of the provided negative value will be freed. This parameter can be NULL if cReserveRecords is zero and must be NULL if the CLFS_FLAG_USE_RESERVATION flag of fFlags is set.

params.name: fFlags
params.description: This parameter can be any combination of the following flags.

params.name: plsn
params.description: A pointer to a CLFS_LSN structure that receives the LSN of the appended record. This parameter can be NULL if cWriteEntries is zero.

returns.description: ClfsReserveAndAppendLogAligned returns STATUS_SUCCESS if it succeeds; otherwise, it returns one of the error codes defined in Ntstatus.h.

functions.name: ClfsScanLogContainers
functions.summary: The ClfsScanLogContainers function retrieves descriptive information for a sequence of containers that belong to a particular CLFS log.

params.name: pcxScan
params.description: A pointer to a CLFS_SCAN_CONTEXT structure. The caller previously allocated the structure and initialized it by calling ClfsCreateScanContext. In particular, the pInfoContainer member was initialized to point to an array of CLFS_CONTAINER_INFORMATION structures, and the cContainers member was initialized to the number of elements in the array. On return, the structures in the array receive descriptive information for the containers in the sequence.

params.name: eScanMode
params.description: A set of flags that specify the direction of the scan and whether the scan context should be closed. The following flags are available to callers of this function.

returns.description: ClfsScanLogContainers returns STATUS_SUCCESS if it succeeds; otherwise, it returns one of the error codes defined in Ntstatus.h.

functions.name: ClfsSetArchiveTail
functions.summary: The ClfsSetArchiveTail function sets the archive tail of a CLFS log to a specified LSN.

params.name: plfoLog
params.description: A pointer to a LOG_FILE_OBJECT structure that represents a CLFS log. The caller previously obtained this pointer by calling ClfsCreateLogFile.

params.name: plsnArchiveTail
params.description: A pointer to a CLFS_LSN structure that specifies the LSN that is to become the new archive tail. This must be the exact LSN of a record in the log.

returns.description: ClfsSetArchiveTail returns STATUS_SUCCESS if it succeeds; otherwise, it returns one of the error codes defined in Ntstatus.h.

functions.name: ClfsSetEndOfLog
functions.summary: The ClfsSetEndOfLog function truncates a CLFS stream.

params.name: plfoLog
params.description: A pointer to a LOG_FILE_OBJECT structure that represents a CLFS stream. This stream must be the only stream of a dedicated log. The caller previously obtained this pointer by calling ClfsCreateLogFile.

params.name: plsnEnd
params.description: A pointer to a CLFS_LSN structure that supplies the LSN of the record that is to become the last record of the stream. This must be the exact LSN of one of the records in the stream.

returns.description: ClfsSetEndOfLog returns STATUS_SUCCESS if it succeeds; otherwise, it returns one of the error codes defined in Ntstatus.h.

functions.name: ClfsSetLogFileInformation
functions.summary: The ClfsSetLogFileInformation function sets metadata and state information for a specified stream and its underlying physical log.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS ClfsSetLogFileInformation(PLOG_FILE_OBJECT plfoLog, CLFS_LOG_INFORMATION_CLASS eInformationClass, PVOID pinfoBuffer, ULONG cbBuffer);

params.name: plfoLog
params.description: A pointer to a LOG_FILE_OBJECT structure that represents a CLFS stream. The caller previously obtained this pointer by calling ClfsCreateLogFile.

params.name: eInformationClass
params.description: A CLFS_LOG_INFORMATION_CLASS value that specifies the class of information being set.

params.name: pinfoBuffer
params.description: A pointer to a buffer that supplies the log information. The structure of this buffer varies according to the class of information specified by eInformationClass. The following table shows the relationship between the information class and the buffer type.

params.name: cbBuffer
params.description: The size, in bytes, of the buffer pointed to by pinfoBuffer.

returns.description: ClfsSetLogFileInformation returns STATUS_SUCCESS if it succeeds; otherwise, it returns one of the error codes defined in Ntstatus.h.

functions.name: ClfsTerminateReadLog
functions.summary: The ClfsTerminateReadLog function invalidates a specified read context after freeing resources associated with the context.

params.name: pvCursorContext
params.description: A pointer to the read context to be invalidated. The caller previously obtained this pointer by calling ClfsReadLogRecord or ClfsReadRestartArea.

returns.description: ClfsTerminateReadLog returns STATUS_SUCCESS if it succeeds; otherwise, it returns one of the error codes defined in Ntstatus.h.

functions.name: ClfsWriteRestartArea
functions.summary: The ClfsWriteRestartArea function atomically appends a new restart record to a CLFS stream, flushes the restart record to stable storage, and optionally updates the base LSN of the stream.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS ClfsWriteRestartArea(PVOID pvMarshalContext, PVOID pvRestartBuffer, ULONG cbRestartBuffer, PCLFS_LSN plsnBase, ULONG fFlags, PULONG pcbWritten, PCLFS_LSN plsnNext);

params.name: pvMarshalContext
params.description: A pointer to an opaque context that represents a marshalling area associated with a CLFS stream. The caller previously obtained this pointer by calling ClfsCreateMarshallingArea.

params.name: pvRestartBuffer
params.description: A pointer to a buffer that contains the data for the restart record.

params.name: cbRestartBuffer
params.description: The size, in bytes, of the buffer pointed to by pvRestartBuffer. This is the size of the restart data.

params.name: plsnBase
params.description: A pointer to a CLFS_LSN structure that specifies a new base LSN for the stream. If this parameter is NULL, the base LSN is not changed.

params.name: fFlags
params.description: This parameter must be one of the following values.

params.name: pcbWritten
params.description: A pointer to a ULONG-typed variable that receives the number of bytes actually forced to stable storage. This parameter can be NULL.

params.name: plsnNext
params.description: A pointer to a CLFS_LSN structure that receives the LSN of the newly written restart record.

returns.description: ClfsWriteRestartArea returns STATUS_SUCCESS if it succeeds; otherwise, it returns one of the error codes defined in Ntstatus.h.

functions.name: CmCallbackGetKeyObjectID
functions.summary: The CmCallbackGetKeyObjectID function retrieves the unique identifier and object name that are associated with a specified registry key object.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS CmCallbackGetKeyObjectID(PLARGE_INTEGER Cookie, PVOID Object, PULONG_PTR ObjectID, PCUNICODE_STRING * ObjectName);

params.name: Cookie
params.description: The cookie value that the driver previously obtained by calling the CmRegisterCallback or CmRegisterCallbackEx function.

params.name: Object
params.description: The pointer value that the driver's RegistryCallback callback function received in the Object member of one of the REG_*XXX*_KEY_INFORMATION structures.

params.name: ObjectID
params.description: A pointer to a location that receives a pointer to the unique identifier that represents the registry key that *Object* specifies. This parameter is optional and can be NULL.

params.name: ObjectName
params.description: A pointer to a location that receives a pointer to a UNICODE_STRING structure. This structure contains the object name of the registry key object that *Object* specifies. The object name is actually the full path name of the registry key that the object represents. The caller must not write to this UNICODE_STRING structure or free it. This parameter is optional and can be NULL.

returns.description: CmCallbackGetKeyObjectID returns STATUS_SUCCESS if the operation succeeds. Possible error return values include the following status code.

functions.name: CmCallbackGetKeyObjectIDEx
functions.summary: The CmCallbackGetKeyObjectIDEx function retrieves the unique identifier and object name that are associated with a specified registry key object.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS CmCallbackGetKeyObjectIDEx(PLARGE_INTEGER Cookie, PVOID Object, PULONG_PTR ObjectID, PCUNICODE_STRING * ObjectName, ULONG Flags);

params.name: Cookie
params.description: A cookie value that represents the caller's registration to receive registry filter callbacks. The driver previously obtained this cookie value from the CmRegisterCallback or CmRegisterCallbackEx function.

params.name: Object
params.description: A pointer to the registry key object. This parameter is the pointer value that the driver's RegistryCallback callback function received in the Object member of one of the REG_*XXX*_KEY_INFORMATION structures.

params.name: ObjectID
params.description: A pointer to a location that receives a pointer to the key identifier for the registry key that *Object* represents. This identifier is unique across all keys in the registry. This parameter is optional and can be NULL. For more information, see the Remarks section below..

params.name: ObjectName
params.description: A pointer to a location that receives a pointer to a UNICODE_STRING structure. This structure contains the object name of the registry key object that *Object* specifies. The object name is actually the full path name of the registry key that the object represents. The caller is responsible for freeing this structure by calling the CmCallbackReleaseKeyObjectIDEx function. This parameter is optional and can be NULL. For more information, see Remarks.

params.name: Flags
params.description: Reserved. Set to zero.

returns.description: CmCallbackGetKeyObjectIDEx returns STATUS_SUCCESS if the operation succeeds. Possible error return values include the following status code:

functions.name: CmCallbackReleaseKeyObjectIDEx
functions.summary: The CmCallbackReleaseKeyObjectIDEx function frees an object name string obtained from the CmCallbackGetKeyObjectIDEx function.

params.name: ObjectName
params.description: A pointer to a UNICODE_STRING structure that contains the object name string. The driver previously obtained this pointer by calling CmCallbackGetKeyObjectIDEx.

returns.description: None

functions.name: CmGetBoundTransaction
functions.summary: The CmGetBoundTransaction function returns a pointer to the transaction object that represents the transaction, if any, that is associated with a specified registry key object.

params.name: Cookie

params.name: Object
params.description: The pointer value that the driver's RegistryCallback callback function received in one of the REG_XXX_KEY_INFORMATION structures.

returns.description: CmGetBoundTransaction returns a pointer to a transaction object, if the key object that the Object parameter specifies is associated with a transaction. Otherwise, the function returns NULL.

functions.name: CmGetCallbackVersion
functions.summary: The CmGetCallbackVersion function retrieves the major and minor version numbers for the current version of the configuration manager's registry callback feature.

params.name: Minor
params.description: A pointer to a location that receives the minor version number.

returns.description: None

functions.name: CmRegisterCallback
functions.summary: The CmRegisterCallback function is obsolete for Windows Vista and later operating system versions. Use CmRegisterCallbackEx instead.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS CmRegisterCallback(PEX_CALLBACK_FUNCTION Function, PVOID Context, PLARGE_INTEGER Cookie);

params.name: Function
params.description: A pointer to the RegistryCallback function to register.

params.name: Context
params.description: A driver-defined value that the configuration manager will pass as the CallbackContext parameter to the RegistryCallback function

params.name: Cookie
params.description: A pointer to a LARGE_INTEGER variable that receives the value that identifies the callback function. When you unregister the callback function, pass this value as the Cookie parameter to CmUnRegisterCallback.

returns.description: CmRegisterCallback returns STATUS_SUCCESS if the operation succeeds or the appropriate NTSTATUS error code if it fails.

functions.name: CmRegisterCallbackEx
functions.summary: The CmRegisterCallbackEx function registers a RegistryCallback function.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS CmRegisterCallbackEx(PEX_CALLBACK_FUNCTION Function, PCUNICODE_STRING Altitude, PVOID Driver, PVOID Context, PLARGE_INTEGER Cookie, PVOID Reserved);

params.name: Function
params.description: A pointer to the RegistryCallback function to register.

params.name: Altitude
params.description: A pointer to a UNICODE_STRING structure. This structure must contain a string that represents the altitude of the calling minifilter driver. For more information, see Remarks.

params.name: Driver
params.description: A pointer to the DRIVER_OBJECT structure that represents the driver.

params.name: Context
params.description: A driver-defined value that the configuration manager will pass as the CallbackContext parameter to the RegistryCallback function.

params.name: Cookie
params.description: A pointer to a LARGE_INTEGER variable that receives the value that identifies the callback function. When you unregister the callback function, pass this value as the Cookie parameter to CmUnRegisterCallback.

params.name: Reserved
params.description: This parameter is reserved for future use.

returns.description: CmRegisterCallbackEx returns STATUS_SUCCESS if the operation succeeds. Otherwise, this function might return one of the following NTSTATUS values:

functions.name: CmSetCallbackObjectContext
functions.summary: The CmSetCallbackObjectContext function associates new context information with a specified registry object and callback function.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS CmSetCallbackObjectContext(PVOID Object, PLARGE_INTEGER Cookie, PVOID NewContext, PVOID * OldContext);

params.name: Object
params.description: A pointer to the registry key object that the driver is providing context information for. The driver obtains this pointer from the ResultObject member of one of the following structures:

params.name: Cookie
params.description: A pointer to a LARGE_INTEGER value that identifies the callback function to associate the context with. The CmRegisterCallbackEx function provided this value when you registered the callback function.

params.name: NewContext
params.description: A pointer to driver-defined context information.

params.name: OldContext
params.description: A pointer to a location that receives a pointer to context information that the driver previously associated with the specified object and cookie. This parameter is optional and can be NULL.

returns.description: CmSetCallbackObjectContext returns STATUS_SUCCESS or another appropriate NTSTATUS-typed value.

functions.name: CmUnRegisterCallback
functions.summary: The CmUnRegisterCallback function unregisters a RegistryCallback function that a CmRegisterCallback or CmRegisterCallbackEx function previously registered.

params.name: Cookie
params.description: A LARGE_INTEGER value that identifies the callback function to unregister. CmRegisterCallback provided this value when you registered the callback function.

returns.description: CmUnRegisterCallback returns STATUS_SUCCESS if it succeeds or the appropriate NTSTATUS error code if it fails. If the *Cookie* parameter does not match any registered callback functions, CmUnRegisterCallback returns STATUS_INVALID_PARAMETER.

functions.name: DbgBreakPointWithStatus
functions.summary: The DbgBreakPointWithStatus function breaks into the kernel debugger and sends the value of Status to the debugger.

params.name: Status
params.description: Specifies a ULONG value that is sent to the debugger (for example, a status code or an address).

returns.description: None

functions.name: DbgPrint
functions.summary: The DbgPrint function sends a message to the kernel debugger when the conditions that you specify apply (see the Remarks section below).

params.name: Format
params.description: Specifies a pointer to the format string to print. The *Format* string supports most of the printf-style format specification fields. However, the Unicode format codes (%C, %S, %lc, %ls, %wc, %ws, and %wZ) can only be used with IRQL = PASSIVE_LEVEL. The DbgPrint function does not support any of the floating point types (%f, %e, %E, %g, %G, %a, or %A).

returns.description: If successful, DbgPrint returns the NTSTATUS code STATUS_SUCCESS; otherwise it returns the appropriate error code.

functions.name: DbgPrintEx
functions.summary: The DbgPrintEx function sends a string to the kernel debugger if the conditions you specify are met.
functions.signature: ULONG DbgPrintEx(ULONG ComponentId, ULONG Level, PCSTR Format);

params.name: ComponentId
params.description: Specifies the component calling this function. This must be one of the component name filter IDs defined in the Dpfilter.h header file. To avoid mixing your driver's output with the output of Windows components, you should use only the following values for ComponentId:

params.name: Level
params.description: Specifies the severity of the message being sent. This can be any 32-bit integer. Values between 0 and 31 (inclusive) are treated differently than values between 32 and 0xFFFFFFFF. For details, see Reading and Filtering Debugging Messages.

params.name: Format
params.description: Specifies a pointer to the format string to print. The Format string supports most of the printf-style format specification fields. However, the Unicode format codes (%C, %S, %lc, %ls, %wc, %ws, and %wZ) can only be used with IRQL = PASSIVE_LEVEL. The DbgPrintEx function does not support any of the floating point types (%f, %e, %E, %g, %G, %a, or %A).

returns.description: If successful, DbgPrintEx returns the NTSTATUS code STATUS_SUCCESS; otherwise, it returns the appropriate error code.

functions.name: EtwActivityIdControl
functions.summary: The EtwActivityIdControl function creates, queries, and sets the current activity identifier.

params.name: ControlCode
params.description: The *ControlCode* parameter can be one of the following defined values.

params.name: ActivityId
params.description: The identifier that indicates the activity associated with the event. The *ActivityId* parameter provides a way to group related events and is used in end-to-end tracing.

returns.description: EtwActivityIdControl returns STATUS_SUCCESS or an appropriate NTSTATUS value.

functions.name: EtwEventEnabled
functions.summary: The EtwEventEnabled function verifies whether an event is enabled.

params.name: RegHandle
params.description: A pointer to the event provider registration handle, which is returned by the EtwRegister function if the event provider registration is successful.

params.name: EventDescriptor
params.description: A pointer to a constant EVENT_DESCRIPTOR.

returns.description: The EtwEventEnabled function returns TRUE if the event is enabled and FALSE if the event is not enabled.

functions.name: EtwProviderEnabled
functions.summary: The EtwProviderEnabled function verifies that a provider is enabled for event logging at a specified level and keyword.
functions.signature: BOOLEAN EtwProviderEnabled(REGHANDLE RegHandle, UCHAR Level, ULONGLONG Keyword);

params.name: RegHandle
params.description: A pointer to the event provider registration handle, which is returned by the EtwRegister function if the event provider registration is successful.

params.name: Level
params.description: The level at which the provider is enabled.

params.name: Keyword
params.description: The keyword that indicates whether the provider is enabled.

returns.description: The function returns TRUE if the provider is enabled and FALSE if the provider is not enabled.

functions.name: EtwRegister
functions.summary: The EtwRegister function registers the event provider and must be called before a provider can start tracing. The EtwRegister function is the kernel mode counterpart to the user-mode EventRegister function. The function can also provide a pointer to an optional callback function that can be used to provide additional event filtering capabilities.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS EtwRegister(LPCGUID ProviderId, PETWENABLECALLBACK EnableCallback, PVOID CallbackContext, PREGHANDLE RegHandle);

params.name: ProviderId
params.description: A pointer to the event provider GUID.

params.name: EnableCallback
params.description: A pointer to an optional callback function. The callback function provides additional event filtering capabilities. The callback function is user-defined.

params.name: CallbackContext
params.description: The function passes back the optional callback context when a callback is made. You can specify the optional context when you register a provider. The CallbackContext parameter supports the scenarios in which one callback is shared by multiple providers, as in a C++ class. The CallbackContext provides a way to distinguish the target provider instances for the enable callback.

params.name: RegHandle
params.description: A pointer to a variable that receives the provider registration handle if the function call is successful.

returns.description: The EtwRegister function returns a status code from the following list:

functions.name: EtwSetInformation
functions.summary: The EtwSetInformation provides special-purpose information to modify a kernel-mode ETW provider registration. The EtwSetInformation function is the kernel-mode equivalent of the EventSetInformation function.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS EtwSetInformation(REGHANDLE RegHandle, EVENT_INFO_CLASS InformationClass, PVOID EventInformation, ULONG InformationLength);

params.name: RegHandle
params.description: The registration handle of the ETW provider to modify. The registration handle is returned by EtwRegister.

params.name: InformationClass
params.description: The type (EVENT_INFO_CLASS) of operation to perform on the registration object.

params.name: EventInformation
params.description: The input buffer.

params.name: InformationLength
params.description: Size of the input buffer.

returns.description: If the function succeeds, the return value is STATUS_SUCCESS.

functions.name: EtwUnregister
functions.summary: The EtwUnregister function unregisters the event provider and must be called before the provider exits.

params.name: RegHandle
params.description: A pointer to the provider registration handle, which is returned by the EtwRegister function if the event provider registration is successful.

returns.description: The EtwUnregister function returns a status code of STATUS_SUCCESS if the event provider was successfully unregistered with ETW.

functions.name: EtwWrite
functions.summary: The EtwWrite function is a tracing function for publishing events in your kernel-mode driver code.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS EtwWrite(REGHANDLE RegHandle, PCEVENT_DESCRIPTOR EventDescriptor, LPCGUID ActivityId, ULONG UserDataCount, PEVENT_DATA_DESCRIPTOR UserData);

params.name: RegHandle
params.description: A pointer to the event provider registration handle, which is returned by the EtwRegister function if the event provider registration is successful.

params.name: EventDescriptor
params.description: A pointer to the EVENT_DESCRIPTOR structure.

params.name: ActivityId
params.description: The identifier that indicates the activity associated with the event. The *ActivityID* provides a way to group related events and is used in end-to-end tracing.

params.name: UserDataCount
params.description: The number of EVENT_DATA_DESCRIPTOR structures in *UserData*.

params.name: UserData
params.description: A pointer to the array of EVENT_DATA_DESCRIPTOR structures.

returns.description: If the event was successfully published, EtwWrite returns STATUS_SUCCESS.

functions.name: EtwWriteEx
functions.summary: The EtwWriteEx function is a tracing function for publishing events that support filtering in your kernel-mode driver code.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS EtwWriteEx(REGHANDLE RegHandle, PCEVENT_DESCRIPTOR EventDescriptor, ULONG64 Filter, ULONG Flags, LPCGUID ActivityId, LPCGUID RelatedActivityId, ULONG UserDataCount, PEVENT_DATA_DESCRIPTOR UserData);

params.name: RegHandle
params.description: A pointer to the event provider registration handle, which is returned by the EtwRegister function if the event provider registration is successful.

params.name: EventDescriptor
params.description: A pointer to the EVENT_DESCRIPTOR structure.

params.name: Filter
params.description: The instance identifiers that identify the session to which the event will not written. That is, the value is a mask of sessions which should be excluded from logging (filtered out). Use a bitwise OR to specify multiple identifiers. Set to zero if you do not support filters or if the event is being written to all sessions (no filters failed). For information on getting the identifier for a session, see the FilterData parameter of your EtwEnableCallback callback.

params.name: Flags
params.description: Reserved. Must be zero (0).

params.name: ActivityId
params.description: The identifier that indicates the activity associated with the event. The ActivityID provides a way to group related events and is used in end-to-end tracing. If NULL, ETW gets the identifier from the thread local storage. For details on getting this identifier, see EtwActivityIdControl.

params.name: RelatedActivityId
params.description: Activity identifier from the previous component. Use this parameter to link your component's events to the previous component's events. To get the activity identifier that was set for the previous component, see the descriptions for the ControlCode parameter of the EtwActivityIdControl function.

params.name: UserDataCount
params.description: Number of EVENT_DATA_DESCRIPTOR structures in UserData. The maximum number is 128.

params.name: UserData
params.description: A pointer to the array of EVENT_DATA_DESCRIPTOR structures. Set this parameter to NULL if UserDataCount is zero. The data must be in the order specified in the manifest.

returns.description: Returns ERROR_SUCCESS if successful or one of the following values on error.

functions.name: EtwWriteString
functions.summary: The EventWriteString function is a tracing function that you can use when no sophisticated data is required. This function is similar to a debug print statement.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS EtwWriteString(REGHANDLE RegHandle, UCHAR Level, ULONGLONG Keyword, LPCGUID ActivityId, PCWSTR String);

params.name: RegHandle
params.description: A Pointer to the event provider registration handle, which is returned by the EtwRegister function if the event provider registration is successful.

params.name: Level
params.description: The level at which the event is active.

params.name: Keyword
params.description: The keyword for the event. A keyword is a bitmask that makes general statements about the category of the event or error. Because the keyword is a bitmask, you can apply more than one keyword to a single event. You can define the keywords and bit positions, or you can use Windows-standard keywords, or you can use combination of your own keywords and the Windows keywords.

params.name: ActivityId
params.description: The identifier that indicates the activity associated with the event. The ActivityId provides a way to group related events and is used in end-to-end tracing. This identifier is optional and can be NULL.

params.name: String
params.description: A null-terminated string (WCHAR).

returns.description: The function returns STATUS_SUCCESS if the event is published successfully.

functions.name: EtwWriteTransfer
functions.summary: The EtwWriteTransfer function marks an event that links two activities together; this type of event is referred to as a *transfer event*. A transfer event can contain the same user-defined data, the same fields, and is subject to the same rules as other events.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS EtwWriteTransfer(REGHANDLE RegHandle, PCEVENT_DESCRIPTOR EventDescriptor, LPCGUID ActivityId, LPCGUID RelatedActivityId, ULONG UserDataCount, PEVENT_DATA_DESCRIPTOR UserData);

params.name: RegHandle
params.description: A pointer to the event provider registration handle, which is returned by the EtwRegister function if the event provider registration is successful.

params.name: EventDescriptor
params.description: A pointer to the EVENT_DESCRIPTOR structure.

params.name: ActivityId
params.description: The identifier that indicates the activity associated with the event. The *ActivityId* provides a way to group related events and is used in end-to-end tracing. This identifier is optional and can be NULL.

params.name: RelatedActivityId
params.description: The identifier that indicates related activity associated with the event. The *RelatedActivityID* provides a way to group related events and is used in end-to-end tracing.

params.name: UserDataCount
params.description: The number of elements in an array of EVENT_DATA_DESCRIPTOR structures.

params.name: UserData
params.description: The pointer to the first element in an array of EVENT_DATA_DESCRIPTOR structures.

returns.description: EtwWriteTransfer returns STATUS_SUCCESS if the event was successfully published.

functions.name: ExAcquireFastMutex
functions.summary: The ExAcquireFastMutex function acquires the given fast mutex with APCs to the current thread disabled.

returns.description: None

functions.summary: The ExAcquireFastMutexUnsafe function acquires the specified fast mutex for the calling thread.
