functions.name: ExAcquireResourceExclusiveLite
functions.summary: The ExAcquireResourceExclusiveLite function acquires the given resource for exclusive access by the calling thread.

params.name: Resource
params.description: A pointer to the resource to acquire.

params.name: Wait
params.description: Specifies the function's behavior whenever the resource cannot be acquired immediately. If TRUE, the caller is put into a wait state until the resource can be acquired. If FALSE, the function immediately returns, regardless of whether the resource can be acquired.

returns.description: ExAcquireResourceExclusiveLite returns TRUE if the resource is acquired. This function returns FALSE if the input *Wait* is FALSE and exclusive access cannot be granted immediately.

functions.name: ExAcquireResourceSharedLite
functions.summary: The ExAcquireResourceSharedLite function acquires the given resource for shared access by the calling thread.

params.name: Resource
params.description: A pointer to the resource to acquire.

params.name: Wait
params.description: Specifies the function's behavior whenever the resource cannot be acquired immediately. If TRUE, the caller is put into a wait state until the resource can be acquired. If FALSE, the function immediately returns, regardless of whether the resource can be acquired.

returns.description: The caller can release the resource by calling either ExReleaseResourceLite or ExReleaseResourceForThreadLite.

functions.name: ExAcquireRundownProtection
functions.summary: The ExAcquireRundownProtection function tries to acquire run-down protection on a shared object so the caller can safely access the object.

params.name: RunRef
params.description: A pointer to an EX_RUNDOWN_REF structure that was initialized by a previous call to the ExInitializeRundownProtection function. The run-down protection functions use this structure to track the run-down status of the associated shared object. This structure is opaque to drivers.

returns.description: ExAcquireRundownProtection returns TRUE if the function successfully acquires run-down protection for the caller. Otherwise, it returns FALSE. A return value of FALSE indicates that the run down of the object has started and that the object must be treated as invalid.

functions.name: ExAcquireRundownProtectionCacheAware
functions.summary: The ExAcquireRundownProtectionCacheAware function tries to acquire cache-aware run-down protection on a shared object so the caller can safely access the object.

params.name: RunRefCacheAware
params.description: Pointer to the opaque EX_RUNDOWN_REF_CACHE_AWARE structure returned by a previous call to ExAllocateCacheAwareRundownProtection or ExInitializeRundownProtectionCacheAware.

returns.description: Returns TRUE if rundown protection was acquired and FALSE if rundown is currently active or completed.

functions.name: ExAcquireRundownProtectionCacheAwareEx
functions.summary: The ExAcquireRundownProtectionCacheAwareEx function tries to acquire cache-aware run-down protection on a shared object so the caller can safely access the object.

params.name: RunRefCacheAware
params.description: Pointer to the opaque EX_RUNDOWN_REF_CACHE_AWARE structure returned by a previous call to ExAllocateCacheAwareRundownProtection or ExInitializeRundownProtectionCacheAware.

params.name: Count
params.description: The amount by which to increment to the run-down instance count of the object. The count is incremented only if the function returns TRUE. For more information, see Remarks.

returns.description: ExAcquireRundownProtectionCacheAwareEx returns TRUE if the function successfully acquires run-down protection for the caller. Otherwise, it returns FALSE. A return value of FALSE indicates that the run down of the object has started and that the object must be treated as invalid.

functions.name: ExAcquireRundownProtectionEx
functions.summary: The ExAcquireRundownProtectionEx function tries to acquire run-down protection on a shared object so the caller can safely access the object.

params.name: RunRef
params.description: A pointer to an EX_RUNDOWN_REF structure that was initialized by a previous call to the ExInitializeRundownProtection function. The run-down protection functions use this structure to track the run-down status of the associated shared object. This structure is opaque to drivers.

params.name: Count
params.description: The amount by which to increment to the run-down instance count of the object. The count is incremented only if the function returns TRUE. For more information, see Remarks

returns.description: ExAcquireRundownProtectionEx returns TRUE if the function successfully acquires run-down protection for the caller. Otherwise, it returns FALSE. A return value of FALSE indicates that the run down of the object has started and that the object must be treated as invalid.

functions.name: ExAcquireSharedStarveExclusive
functions.summary: The ExAcquireSharedStarveExclusive function acquires a given resource for shared access without waiting for any pending attempts to acquire exclusive access to the same resource.

params.description: A pointer to the resource to be acquired for shared access.

params.name: Wait
params.description: Specifies the function's behavior whenever the resource cannot be acquired immediately. If TRUE, the caller is put into a wait state until the resource can be acquired. If FALSE, the function immediately returns, regardless of whether the resource can be acquired.

functions.name: ExAcquireSharedWaitForExclusive
functions.summary: The ExAcquireSharedWaitForExclusive function acquires the given resource for shared access if shared access can be granted and there are no exclusive waiters.

params.name: Resource
params.description: A pointer to the resource to be acquired for shared access.

params.name: Wait
params.description: Specifies the function's behavior whenever the resource cannot be acquired immediately. If TRUE, the caller is put into a wait state until the resource can be acquired. If FALSE, the function immediately returns, regardless of whether the resource can be acquired.

returns.description: ExAcquireSharedWaitForExclusive returns TRUE if the requested access is granted or an exclusive owner releases the resource. This function returns FALSE if the input Wait is FALSE and shared access cannot be granted immediately.

functions.summary: The ExAcquireSpinLockShared function acquires a spin lock for shared access by the caller, and raises the IRQL to DISPATCH_LEVEL.

functions.summary: The ExAcquireSpinLockSharedAtDpcLevel function acquires a spin lock for shared access by a caller that is already running at IRQL \>= DISPATCH_LEVEL.

functions.name: ExAllocateCacheAwareRundownProtection
functions.summary: The ExAllocateCacheAwareRundownProtection function allocates a cache-friendly rundown protection structure for multi-processor scenarios. Rundown protection is a synchronization mechanism that allows for the safe cleanup of resources that might be accessed by multiple threads.

params.name: PoolTag
params.description: A ULONG that specifies the pool tag for the memory allocation. The pool tag is a 32-bit value that is used to track memory usage.

returns.description: Returns a pointer to an opaque EX_RUNDOWN_REF_CACHE_AWARE structure or NULL if allocation fails.

functions.name: ExAllocateFromLookasideListEx
functions.summary: The ExAllocateFromLookasideListEx function removes the first entry from the specified lookaside list, or, if the list is empty, dynamically allocates the storage for a new entry.

functions.name: ExAllocateFromNPagedLookasideList
functions.summary: The ExAllocateFromNPagedLookasideList function returns a pointer to a nonpaged entry from the given lookaside list, or it returns a pointer to a newly allocated nonpaged entry.

functions.name: ExAllocateFromPagedLookasideList

params.name: Lookaside

returns.description: ExAllocateFromPagedLookasideList returns a pointer to an entry if one can be allocated. Otherwise, it returns NULL.

functions.name: ExAllocatePool
functions.summary: >[!WARNING] > ExAllocatePool is obsolete and has been deprecated in Windows 10, version 2004. It has been replaced by ExAllocatePool2. For more information, see Updating deprecated ExAllocatePool calls to ExAllocatePool2 and ExAllocatePool3. > > When developing drivers for version of Windows prior to Windows 10, version 2004, use ExAllocatePoolZero.

params.name: PoolType
params.description: Specifies the type of pool memory to allocate. For a description of the available pool memory types, see POOL_TYPE.

params.name: NumberOfBytes
params.description: Specifies the number of bytes to allocate.

returns.description: ExAllocatePool returns NULL if there is insufficient memory in the free pool to satisfy the request. Otherwise the function returns a pointer to the allocated memory.

functions.name: ExAllocatePool2
functions.summary: The ExAllocatePool2 function allocates pool memory of the specified type and returns a pointer to the allocated block.
functions.signature: PVOID ExAllocatePool2(POOL_FLAGS Flags, SIZE_T NumberOfBytes, ULONG Tag);

params.name: Flags
params.description: A ULONG64-typed value specifying the type of pool memory along with required and optional attributes. Multiple flag values can be combined using bit-wise OR. See POOL_FLAGS for possible values.

params.name: NumberOfBytes
params.description: Specifies a non-zero number of bytes to allocate.

params.name: Tag
params.description: The pool tag to use for the allocated memory. Specify the pool tag as a non-zero character literal of one to four characters delimited by single quotation marks (for example, `Tag1`). The string is usually specified in reverse order (for example, `1gaT`). Each ASCII character in the tag must be a value in the range 0x20 (space) to 0x7E (tilde). Each allocation code path should use a unique pool tag to help debuggers and verifiers identify the code path.

functions.name: ExAllocatePool3

functions.name: ExInitializeLookasideListEx
functions.summary: The ExInitializeLookasideListEx function initializes a lookaside list.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS ExInitializeLookasideListEx(PLOOKASIDE_LIST_EX Lookaside, PALLOCATE_FUNCTION_EX Allocate, PFREE_FUNCTION_EX Free, POOL_TYPE PoolType, ULONG Flags, SIZE_T Size, ULONG Tag, USHORT Depth);

params.name: Lookaside
params.description: A pointer to the LOOKASIDE_LIST_EX structure to initialize. On return, this structure describes an empty lookaside list. The caller must use nonpaged system space for this structure, regardless of whether the entries in the lookaside list are allocated from paged or nonpaged memory. On 64-bit platforms, this structure must be 16-byte aligned.

params.name: Allocate
params.description: A pointer to a caller-supplied LookasideListAllocateEx function that allocates a new lookaside-list entry. The ExAllocateFromLookasideListEx function calls this *LookasideListAllocateEx* function if the lookaside list is empty (contains no entries). This parameter is optional and can be specified as NULL if a custom allocation function is not required. If this parameter is NULL, calls to ExAllocateFromPagedLookasideList automatically allocate the paged or nonpaged storage (as determined by the *PoolType* parameter) for the new entries.

params.name: Free
params.description: A pointer to a caller-supplied LookasideListFreeEx function that frees a previously allocated lookaside-list entry. The ExFreeToPagedLookasideList function calls this *LookasideListFreeEx* function if the lookaside list is full (that is, the list already contains the maximum number of entries, as determined by the operating system). This parameter is optional and can be specified as NULL if a custom deallocation function is not required. If this parameter is NULL, calls to ExFreeToPagedLookasideList automatically free the storage for the specified entries.

params.name: PoolType
params.description: Specifies the pool type of the entries in the lookaside list. Set this parameter to a valid POOL_TYPE enumeration value.

params.name: Flags
params.description: Specifies an optional flag value to modify the default behavior of the *LookasideListAllocateEx* function. Set this parameter to zero or to one of the following EX_LOOKASIDE_LIST_EX_FLAGS_*XXX* flag bits.

params.name: Size
params.description: Specifies the size, in bytes, of each entry in the lookaside list.

params.name: Tag
params.description: Specifies the four-byte pool tag to use to mark the allocated storage for lookaside-list entries. For more information about pool tags, see the description of the *Tag* parameter in ExAllocatePoolWithTag.

params.description: A pointer to an executive resource (an opaque ERESOURCE structure) that is owned by the calling thread. The caller previously allocated this structure and initialized it by calling the ExInitializeResourceLite function. For more information, see the following Remarks section.

params.name: OwnerPointer
params.description: A pointer value that identifies the resource owner. This parameter value is nominally a pointer to a value of type ERESOURCE_THREAD but is cast to type PVOID. The caller must set the two least significant bits of this pointer value to ones. For more information, see the following Remarks section.

params.name: Flags
params.description: A set of flags that can modify the operation of this function. Set this parameter either to zero or to the following flag value:

functions.name: ExSetTimer
functions.summary: The ExSetTimer function starts a timer operation and sets the timer to expire at the specified due time.
functions.signature: BOOLEAN ExSetTimer(PEX_TIMER Timer, LONGLONG DueTime, LONGLONG Period, PEXT_SET_PARAMETERS Parameters);

params.name: Timer
params.description: A pointer to an EX_TIMER structure. This structure is a timer object that was previously allocated by the ExAllocateTimer function.

params.name: DueTime
params.description: The absolute or relative time at which the timer is to expire. If the value of the DueTime parameter is negative, the expiration time is relative to the current system time. Otherwise, the expiration time is absolute. The expiration time is expressed in system time units (100-nanosecond intervals). Absolute expiration times track any changes in the system time; relative expiration times are not affected by system time changes. An absolute time is expressed as the amount of time passed, in system time units, since the start of the year 1601.

params.name: Period
params.description: An optional period for the timer in system time units (100-nanosecond intervals). Must be less than or equal to MAXLONG. For a timer that is one-shot instead of periodic, set Period to zero.

params.name: Parameters
params.description: A pointer to an EXT_SET_PARAMETERS structure. The calling driver previously called the ExInitializeSetTimerParameters function to initialize this structure.

returns.description: This function returns TRUE if it cancels a timer that was pending at the time that the function was called. Otherwise, the function returns FALSE. For more information, see Remarks.

functions.name: ExSetTimerResolution
functions.summary: The ExSetTimerResolution function modifies the frequency at which the system clock interrupts. Use this function with extreme caution (see the following Remarks section).

params.name: DesiredTime
params.description: Specifies the amount of time that should elapse between each timer interrupt, in 100-nanosecond units. The minimum value is approximately 10,000 (1 millisecond) but can vary slightly by platform. (This parameter is ignored if *SetResolution* is FALSE.)

params.name: SetResolution
params.description: If TRUE, the call is a request to set the clock interrupt frequency to the value specified by *DesiredTime*. If FALSE, the call is a request to restore the clock interrupt frequency to the system's default value, which is platform-specific.

returns.description: ExSetTimerResolution returns the new timer resolution, in 100-nanosecond units.

functions.name: IoAllocateErrorLogEntry
functions.summary: The IoAllocateErrorLogEntry function allocates an error log entry, and returns a pointer to the packet that the caller uses to supply information about an I/O error.

params.name: IoObject

params.name: EntrySize
params.description: Specifies the size, in bytes, of the error log entry to be allocated. This value cannot exceed ERROR_LOG_MAXIMUM_SIZE.

returns.description: IoAllocateErrorLogEntry returns a pointer to the error log entry, or NULL if a log entry could not be allocated.

functions.name: IoAllocateIrp
functions.summary: The IoAllocateIrp function allocates an IRP, given the number of I/O stack locations for each driver layered under the caller, and, optionally, for the caller. See also IoAllocateIrpEx.

params.name: StackSize
params.description: Specifies the number of I/O stack locations to be allocated for the IRP. This value must be at least equal to the StackSize of the next-lower driver's device object, but can be one greater than this value. The calling driver need not allocate a stack location in the IRP for itself.

params.name: ChargeQuota
params.description: Setting this to TRUE causes the memory allocated for the IRP to be charged against the quota for the current process. Should be set to FALSE by intermediate drivers. This can be set to TRUE only by highest-level drivers that are called in the context of the thread that originates the I/O request for which the driver is allocating another IRP.

returns.description: IoAllocateIrp returns a pointer to an IRP, which was allocated from nonpaged system space, or NULL if an IRP could not be allocated.

functions.name: IoAllocateIrpEx
functions.summary: IoAllocateIrpEx allocates an IRP from the system nonpaged pool, possibly with an IRP extension.
functions.signature: PIRP IoAllocateIrpEx(PDEVICE_OBJECT DeviceObject, CCHAR StackSize, BOOLEAN ChargeQuota);

params.name: DeviceObject
params.description: Pointer to the device object to check to determine whether to add space for an IRP extension. When DeviceObject is set to DEVICE_WITH_IRP_EXTENSION, space for the IRP extension is also allocated.

params.name: StackSize
params.description: Maximum number of stack locations to be allocated for the IRP. StackSize must be at least equal to the StackSize of the next-lower driver's device object, but can be one greater than this value. The calling driver does not need to allocate a stack location in the IRP for itself.

params.name: ChargeQuota
params.description: Setting ChargeQuota to TRUE causes the memory allocated for the IRP to be charged against the quota for the current process. This parameter can be set TRUE only by the highest-level drivers that are called in the context of the thread that originates the I/O request for which the driver is allocating another IRP. Intermediate drivers should set this parameter to FALSE.

returns.description: IoAllocateIrpEx returns a pointer to the allocated and initialized IRP, or NULL if an IRP could not be allocated.

functions.name: IoAllocateMdl
functions.summary: The IoAllocateMdl function allocates a memory descriptor list (MDL) large enough to map a buffer, given the buffer's starting address and length. Optionally, this function associates the MDL with an IRP.
functions.signature: PMDL IoAllocateMdl(PVOID VirtualAddress, ULONG Length, BOOLEAN SecondaryBuffer, BOOLEAN ChargeQuota, PIRP Irp);

params.name: VirtualAddress
params.description: Pointer to the base virtual address of the buffer the MDL is to describe.

params.name: Length
params.description: Specifies the length, in bytes, of the buffer that the MDL is to describe. For more information, see the following Remarks section.

params.name: SecondaryBuffer
params.description: Indicates whether the buffer is a primary or secondary buffer. This parameter determines how the MDL is to be linked to the IRP. All buffers except the first buffer described by an MDL in an IRP are considered secondary buffers. This field must be FALSE if no IRP is associated with the MDL. For more information, see the following Remarks section.

params.name: ChargeQuota
params.description: Reserved for system use. Drivers must set this parameter to FALSE.

params.name: Irp
params.description: Pointer to an IRP to be associated with the MDL. If the Irp pointer is non-NULL, the allocated MDL is associated with the specified IRP's MDL list, according to the value of SecondaryBuffer.

returns.description: IoAllocateMdl returns a pointer to an MDL, or, if the MDL cannot be allocated, it returns NULL.

functions.name: IoAllocateWorkItem
functions.summary: The IoAllocateWorkItem function allocates a work item.

params.name: DeviceObject

returns.description: IoAllocateWorkItem returns a pointer to the allocated IO_WORKITEM structure. The function returns NULL if sufficient resources do not exist.

functions.summary: The IoAttachDevice function attaches the caller's device object to a named target device object, so that I/O requests bound for the target device are routed first to the caller.

params.name: TargetDevice

params.name: AttachedDevice

returns.description: IoAttachDevice can return one of the following NTSTATUS values:

functions.name: IoAttachDeviceToDeviceStack
functions.summary: The IoAttachDeviceToDeviceStack function attaches the caller's device object to the highest device object in the chain and returns a pointer to the previously highest device object.

params.name: SourceDevice

params.name: TargetDevice
params.description: Pointer to another driver's device object, such as a pointer returned by a preceding call to IoGetDeviceObjectPointer.

returns.description: IoAttachDeviceToDeviceStack returns a pointer to the device object to which the SourceDevice was attached. The returned device object pointer can differ from TargetDevice if TargetDevice had additional drivers layered on top of it.

functions.name: IoBuildAsynchronousFsdRequest
functions.summary: The IoBuildAsynchronousFsdRequest function allocates and sets up an IRP to be sent to lower-level drivers.
functions.signature: PIRP IoBuildAsynchronousFsdRequest(ULONG MajorFunction, PDEVICE_OBJECT DeviceObject, PVOID Buffer, ULONG Length, PLARGE_INTEGER StartingOffset, PIO_STATUS_BLOCK IoStatusBlock);

params.name: MajorFunction
params.description: The major function code to be set in the IRP. This code can be IRP_MJ_PNP, IRP_MJ_READ, IRP_MJ_WRITE, IRP_MJ_FLUSH_BUFFERS, or IRP_MJ_SHUTDOWN.

params.name: DeviceObject
params.description: A pointer to the next-lower driver's device object. This object represents the target device for the read, write, flush, or shutdown operation.

params.name: Buffer
params.description: A pointer to a buffer into which data is read or from which data is written. The value of this argument is NULL for flush and shutdown requests.

params.name: Length
params.description: The length, in bytes, of the buffer pointed to by *Buffer*. For devices such as disks, this value must be an integer multiple of the sector size. Starting with Windows 8, the sector size can be 4,096 or 512 bytes. In earlier versions of Windows, the sector size is always 512 bytes. This parameter is required for read and write requests, but must be zero for flush and shutdown requests.

params.name: StartingOffset
params.description: A pointer to the starting offset on the input/output media. The value of this argument is zero for flush and shutdown requests.

params.name: IoStatusBlock
params.description: A pointer to the address of an I/O status block in which the to-be-called drivers return final status about the requested operation.

returns.description: IoBuildAsynchronousFsdRequest returns a pointer to an IRP, or a NULL pointer if the IRP cannot be allocated.

functions.name: IoBuildDeviceIoControlRequest
functions.summary: The IoBuildDeviceIoControlRequest function allocates and sets up an IRP for a synchronously processed device control request.
functions.signature: PIRP IoBuildDeviceIoControlRequest(ULONG IoControlCode, PDEVICE_OBJECT DeviceObject, PVOID InputBuffer, ULONG InputBufferLength, PVOID OutputBuffer, ULONG OutputBufferLength, BOOLEAN InternalDeviceIoControl, PKEVENT Event, PIO_STATUS_BLOCK IoStatusBlock);

params.name: IoControlCode
params.description: Supplies the I/O control code (IOCTL) to be used in the request. For information about device type-specific I/O control codes, see device type-specific sections in the Windows Driver Kit (WDK).

params.name: DeviceObject
params.description: Supplies a pointer to the DEVICE_OBJECT structure for the next-lower driver's device object, which represents the target device.

params.name: InputBuffer
params.description: Supplies a pointer to an input buffer to be passed to the lower driver, or NULL if the request does not pass input data to lower drivers.

params.name: InputBufferLength
params.description: Supplies the length, in bytes, of the input buffer. If InputBuffer is NULL, InputBufferLength must be zero.

params.name: OutputBuffer
params.description: Supplies a pointer to an output buffer in which the lower driver is to return data, or NULL if the request does not require lower drivers to return data.

params.name: OutputBufferLength
params.description: Supplies the length, in bytes, of the output buffer. If OutputBuffer is NULL, OutputBufferLength must be zero.

params.name: InternalDeviceIoControl
params.description: If TRUE, the function sets the IRP's major function code to IRP_MJ_INTERNAL_DEVICE_CONTROL. Otherwise, the function sets the IRP's major function code to IRP_MJ_DEVICE_CONTROL.

params.name: Event
params.description: Supplies a pointer to a caller-allocated and initialized event object. The I/O manager sets the event to the Signaled state when a lower-level driver completes the requested operation. After calling IoCallDriver, the driver can wait for the event object. The Event parameter is optional and can be set to NULL. However, if Event is NULL, the caller must supply an IoCompletion function for the IRP to notify the caller when the operation completes.

params.name: IoStatusBlock
params.description: Specifies an I/O status block to be set when the request is completed by lower drivers.

returns.description: If the operation succeeds, IoBuildDeviceIoControlRequest returns a pointer to an IRP, with the next-lower driver's I/O stack location set up from the supplied parameters. Otherwise, the function returns NULL.

functions.name: IoBuildPartialMdl
functions.summary: The IoBuildPartialMdl function builds a new memory descriptor list (MDL) that represents part of a buffer that is described by an existing MDL.
functions.signature: void IoBuildPartialMdl(PMDL SourceMdl, PMDL TargetMdl, PVOID VirtualAddress, ULONG Length);

params.name: SourceMdl
params.description: A pointer to an MDL that describes the original buffer, of which a subrange is to be mapped.

params.name: TargetMdl
params.description: A pointer to a caller-allocated MDL. This MDL must be large enough to describe the pages in the subrange that are specified by VirtualAddress and Length.

params.name: VirtualAddress
params.description: A pointer to the base virtual address for the subrange to be described by the TargetMdl.

params.name: Length
params.description: Specifies the length, in bytes, to be mapped by the TargetMdl. This value, in combination with VirtualAddress, must specify a buffer that is a proper subrange of the buffer that is described by SourceMdl. If Length is zero, the subrange to be mapped starts at VirtualAddress and includes the remaining range described by the SourceMdl.

returns.description: No value.

functions.name: IoBuildSynchronousFsdRequest
functions.summary: The IoBuildSynchronousFsdRequest function allocates and sets up an IRP for a synchronously processed I/O request.
functions.signature: PIRP IoBuildSynchronousFsdRequest(ULONG MajorFunction, PDEVICE_OBJECT DeviceObject, PVOID Buffer, ULONG Length, PLARGE_INTEGER StartingOffset, PKEVENT Event, PIO_STATUS_BLOCK IoStatusBlock);

params.name: MajorFunction
params.description: The major function code for the IRP. This code can be IRP_MJ_PNP, IRP_MJ_READ, IRP_MJ_WRITE, IRP_MJ_FLUSH_BUFFERS, or IRP_MJ_SHUTDOWN.

params.name: DeviceObject
params.description: A pointer to the DEVICE_OBJECT structure for the next-lower driver's device object, which represents the target device.

params.name: Buffer
params.description: A pointer to a data buffer. If MajorFunction is IRP_MJ_WRITE, the buffer contains data to be written. If MajorFunction is IRP_MJ_READ, the buffer receives data. If MajorFunction is IRP_MJ_FLUSH_BUFFERS or IRP_MJ_SHUTDOWN, this parameter must be NULL.

params.name: Length
params.description: The length, in bytes, of the buffer pointed to by Buffer. For devices such as disks, this value must be an integer multiple of the sector size. Starting with Windows 8, the sector size can be 4,096 or 512 bytes. In earlier versions of Windows, the sector size is always 512 bytes. This parameter is required for read and write requests, but must be zero for flush and shutdown requests.

params.name: StartingOffset
params.description: A pointer to the offset on the disk, for read and write requests. The units and meaning of this value are driver-specific. This parameter is required for read and write requests, but must be zero for flush and shutdown requests.

params.name: Event
params.description: A pointer to a caller-allocated and initialized event object. The I/O manager sets the event to the Signaled state when a lower-level driver completes the requested operation. After calling IoCallDriver, the driver can wait for the event object.

params.name: IoStatusBlock
params.description: A pointer to a location that receives the I/O status block that is set when the IRP is completed by a lower-level driver.

returns.description: If the operation succeeds, IoBuildSynchronousFsdRequest returns a pointer to an initialized IRP structure, with the next-lower driver's I/O stack location set up from the supplied parameters. Otherwise, the function returns NULL.

functions.name: IoCancelIrp
functions.summary: The IoCancelIrp function sets the cancel bit in a given IRP and calls the cancel function for the IRP if there is one.

params.name: Irp
params.description: A pointer to the IRP to be canceled.

returns.description: IoCancelIrp returns TRUE if the IRP had a cancel function and this function was called. Otherwise, it returns FALSE. In either case, the IRP's cancel bit is set to TRUE. For more information, see Remarks.

functions.name: IoCheckLinkShareAccess
functions.summary: The IoCheckLinkShareAccess function is called by file system drivers (FSDs) or other highest-level drivers to check whether link shared access to a file object is permitted.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS IoCheckLinkShareAccess(ACCESS_MASK DesiredAccess, ULONG DesiredShareAccess, PFILE_OBJECT FileObject, PSHARE_ACCESS ShareAccess, PLINK_SHARE_ACCESS LinkShareAccess, ULONG IoShareAccessFlags);

params.name: DesiredAccess
params.description: Specifies an ACCESS_MASK value that indicates the desired type of access to the given file object.

params.name: DesiredShareAccess
params.description: Specifies the desired type of shared access to the file object for the current open request. The value of this parameter is usually the same as the ShareAccess parameter that is passed to the file system or highest-level driver by the I/O manager when the open request was made. This value can be zero, or any combination of the following:

params.name: FileObject
params.description: A pointer to the file object for which to check access for the current open request.

params.name: ShareAccess
params.description: A pointer to the common share-access data structure that is associated with FileObject. Drivers should treat this structure as opaque.

params.name: LinkShareAccess
params.description: A pointer to the common link share-access data structure (LINK_SHARE_ACCESS) that is associated with FileObject. Drivers should treat this structure as opaque.

params.name: IoShareAccessFlags
params.description: A bitmask of these flags:

returns.description: The IoCheckLinkShareAccess function returns STATUS_SUCCESS if the requester's access to the file object is compatible with the way in which it is currently open. If the request is denied because of a sharing violation, then STATUS_SHARING_VIOLATION is returned.

functions.name: IoCheckShareAccess
functions.summary: The IoCheckShareAccess function is called by file system drivers (FSDs) or other highest-level drivers to check whether shared access to a file object is permitted.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS IoCheckShareAccess(ACCESS_MASK DesiredAccess, ULONG DesiredShareAccess, PFILE_OBJECT FileObject, PSHARE_ACCESS ShareAccess, BOOLEAN Update);

params.name: DesiredAccess
params.description: Specifies an ACCESS_MASK value that indicates the desired type of access to the given FileObject for the current open request. Drivers compute the value of this parameter by taking the requested access in the IRP_MJ_CREATE request and then applying SeAccessCheck for each security descriptor to determine the actual access granted. If the granted access is more restrictive than the desired access, then that is an error, and the driver should complete the current IRP with a status of STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED. (Note that SeAccessCheck clears the MAXIMUM_ALLOWED bit in the granted access; be sure to not use that bit when comparing desired access to granted access.) The driver then passes the granted access as the value of DesiredAccess.

params.name: DesiredShareAccess
params.description: Specifies the desired type of shared access to FileObject for the current open request. The value of this parameter is usually the same as the ShareAccess passed to the file system or highest-level driver by the I/O manager when the open request was made. This value can be zero, or any combination of the following:

params.name: FileObject
params.description: Pointer to the file object for which to check access for the current open request.

params.name: ShareAccess
params.description: Pointer to the common share-access data structure associated with FileObject. Drivers should treat this structure as opaque.

params.name: Update
params.description: Specifies whether to update the share-access status for FileObject. A Boolean value of TRUE means this function will update the share access information for the file object if the open request is permitted.

returns.description: IoCheckShareAccess returns STATUS_SUCCESS if the requester's access to the file object is compatible with the way in which it is currently open. If the request is denied because of a sharing violation, then STATUS_SHARING_VIOLATION is returned.

functions.name: IoCheckShareAccessEx
functions.summary: The IoCheckShareAccessEx function is called by file system drivers (FSDs) or other highest-level drivers to check whether shared access to a file object is permitted.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS IoCheckShareAccessEx(ACCESS_MASK DesiredAccess, ULONG DesiredShareAccess, PFILE_OBJECT FileObject, PSHARE_ACCESS ShareAccess, BOOLEAN Update, PBOOLEAN WritePermission);

params.name: DesiredAccess
params.description: Specifies an ACCESS_MASK value that indicates the desired type of access to the given file object.

params.name: DesiredShareAccess
params.description: Specifies the desired type of shared access to the file object for the current open request. The value of this parameter is usually the same as the ShareAccess parameter that is passed to the file system or highest-level driver by the I/O manager when the open request was made. This value can be zero, or any combination of the following:

params.name: FileObject
params.description: A pointer to the file object for which to check access for the current open request.

params.name: ShareAccess
params.description: A pointer to the common share-access data structure that is associated with FileObject. Drivers should treat this structure as opaque.

params.name: Update
params.description: Specifies whether to update the share-access status for FileObject. A Boolean value of TRUE means this function will update the share access information for the file object if the open request is permitted.

params.name: WritePermission
params.description: Specifies whether the share access has write permission. This value is TRUE if the share has write permission; otherwise, FALSE. If the value is FALSE and the share access has write permission and the caller attempts to take exclusive read access, the write permission is downgraded to FILE_SHARE_READ. This value is NULL if a write permission check is not done on the share access.

returns.description: The IoCheckShareAccessEx function returns STATUS_SUCCESS if the requester's access to the file object is compatible with the way in which it is currently open. If the request is denied because of a sharing violation, then STATUS_SHARING_VIOLATION is returned.

functions.name: IoConnectInterrupt
functions.summary: The IoConnectInterrupt function registers a device driver's InterruptService function (ISR), so that it will be called when a device interrupts on any of a specified set of processors.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS IoConnectInterrupt(PKINTERRUPT * InterruptObject, PKSERVICE_ROUTINE ServiceRoutine, PVOID ServiceContext, PKSPIN_LOCK SpinLock, ULONG Vector, KIRQL Irql, KIRQL SynchronizeIrql, KINTERRUPT_MODE InterruptMode, BOOLEAN ShareVector, KAFFINITY ProcessorEnableMask, BOOLEAN FloatingSave);

params.name: InterruptObject
params.description: Pointer to the address of driver-supplied storage for a pointer to a set of interrupt objects. This pointer must be passed in subsequent calls to KeSynchronizeExecution.

params.name: ServiceRoutine
params.description: Pointer to the entry point for the driver-supplied InterruptService function.

params.name: ServiceContext
params.description: Pointer to the driver-determined context that will be supplied to the InterruptService function when it is called. The ServiceContext area must be in resident memory: in the device extension of a driver-created device object, in the controller extension of a driver-created controller object, or in nonpaged pool allocated by the device driver. See Providing ISR Context Information for details.

params.name: SpinLock
params.description: Pointer to an initialized spin lock, for which the driver supplies the storage, that will be used to synchronize access to driver-determined data shared by other driver functions. This parameter is required if the ISR handles more than one vector or if the driver has more than one ISR. Otherwise, the driver need not allocate storage for an interrupt spin lock and the input pointer is NULL.

params.name: Vector
params.description: Specifies the interrupt vector passed in the interrupt resource at the u.Interrupt.Vector member of CM_PARTIAL_RESOURCE_DESCRIPTOR.

params.name: Irql
params.description: Specifies the DIRQL passed in the interrupt resource at the u.Interrupt.Level member of CM_PARTIAL_RESOURCE_DESCRIPTOR.

params.name: SynchronizeIrql
params.description: Specifies the DIRQL at which the ISR will run. If the ISR handles more than one interrupt vector or the driver has more than one ISR, this value must be the highest of the Irql values passed at u.Interrupt.Level in each interrupt resource. Otherwise, the Irql and SynchronizeIrql values are identical.

params.name: InterruptMode
params.description: Specifies whether the device interrupt is LevelSensitive or Latched.

params.name: ShareVector
params.description: Specifies whether the interrupt vector is sharable.

params.name: ProcessorEnableMask
params.description: Specifies a KAFFINITY value representing the set of processors on which device interrupts can occur in this platform. This value is passed in the interrupt resource at u.Interrupt.Affinity.

params.name: FloatingSave
params.description: Specifies whether to save the floating-point stack when the driver's device interrupts. For x86-based and Itanium-based platforms, this value must be set to FALSE. For more information about saving floating-point and MMX state, see Using Floating Point or MMX in a WDM Driver.

returns.description: IoConnectInterrupt can return one of the following NTSTATUS values:

functions.summary: For more information, see the WdmlibIoConnectInterruptEx function.

params.name: Parameters
params.description: For more information, see the WdmlibIoConnectInterruptEx function.

returns.description: For more information, see the WdmlibIoConnectInterruptEx function.

functions.name: IoCreateDevice
functions.summary: The IoCreateDevice function creates a device object for use by a driver.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS IoCreateDevice(PDRIVER_OBJECT DriverObject, ULONG DeviceExtensionSize, PUNICODE_STRING DeviceName, ULONG DeviceType, ULONG DeviceCharacteristics, BOOLEAN Exclusive, PDEVICE_OBJECT * DeviceObject);

params.name: DriverObject
params.description: Pointer to the driver object for the caller. Each driver receives a pointer to its driver object in a parameter to its DriverEntry function. WDM function and filter drivers also receive a driver object pointer in their AddDevice functions.

params.name: DeviceExtensionSize
params.description: Specifies the driver-determined number of bytes to be allocated for the device extension of the device object. The internal structure of the device extension is driver-defined.

params.name: DeviceName
params.description: Optionally points to a buffer containing a null-terminated Unicode string that names the device object. The string must be a full path name. WDM filter and function drivers do not name their device objects. For more information, see Named Device Objects.

params.name: DeviceType
params.description: Specifies one of the system-defined FILE_DEVICE_*XXX* constants that indicate the type of device (such as FILE_DEVICE_DISK or FILE_DEVICE_KEYBOARD) or a vendor-defined value for a new type of device. For more information, see Specifying Device Types.

params.name: DeviceCharacteristics
params.description: Specifies one or more system-defined constants, ORed together, that provide additional information about the driver's device. For a list of possible device characteristics, see DEVICE_OBJECT. For more information about how to specify device characteristics, see Specifying Device Characteristics. Most drivers specify FILE_DEVICE_SECURE_OPEN for this parameter.

params.name: Exclusive
params.description: Specifies if the device object represents an exclusive device. Most drivers set this value to FALSE. For more information about exclusive access, see Specifying Exclusive Access to Device Objects.

params.name: DeviceObject
params.description: Pointer to a variable that receives a pointer to the newly created DEVICE_OBJECT structure. The DEVICE_OBJECT structure is allocated from nonpaged pool. The device extension of the device object is zeroed.

returns.description: IoCreateDevice returns STATUS_SUCCESS on success, or the appropriate NTSTATUS error code on failure. A partial list of the failure codes returned by this function includes:

functions.name: IoCreateDriverProxyExtension
functions.summary: The IoCreateDriverProxyExtension function allocates and initializes a DriverProxy extension that enables hot-swappable driver functionality.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS IoCreateDriverProxyExtension(PDRIVER_OBJECT OwningDriverObject, DRIVER_PROXY_EXTENSION_CREATION_FLAGS Flags, PDRIVER_PROXY_EXTENSION * DriverProxyExtension);

params.name: OwningDriverObject
params.description: [in, optional] An optional pointer to the DRIVER_OBJECT that will own the DriverProxy extension. If provided, the extension will be associated with this driver object. If NULL, the extension is created without an owning driver.

params.name: Flags
params.description: [in] A DRIVER_PROXY_EXTENSION_CREATION_FLAGS value that provides additional configuration options for extension creation. Currently, no flags are defined, so this parameter should be set to 0.

params.name: DriverProxyExtension
params.description: [out] A pointer to a variable that receives a pointer to the newly created DriverProxy extension. This extension can be used with other DriverProxy APIs.

returns.description: IoCreateDriverProxyExtension returns one of the following NTSTATUS values:

functions.name: IoCreateFile
functions.summary: The IoCreateFile function either causes a new file or directory to be created, or it opens an existing file, device, directory, or volume, giving the caller a handle for the file object.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS IoCreateFile(PHANDLE FileHandle, ACCESS_MASK DesiredAccess, POBJECT_ATTRIBUTES ObjectAttributes, PIO_STATUS_BLOCK IoStatusBlock, PLARGE_INTEGER AllocationSize, ULONG FileAttributes, ULONG ShareAccess, ULONG Disposition, ULONG CreateOptions, PVOID EaBuffer, ULONG EaLength, CREATE_FILE_TYPE CreateFileType, PVOID InternalParameters, ULONG Options);

params.name: FileHandle
params.description: Pointer to a variable that receives the file handle if the call is successful. The driver must close the handle with ZwClose once the handle is no longer in use.

params.name: DesiredAccess
params.description: A bitmask of flags specifying the type of access to the file or directory that the caller requires. See the *DesiredAccess* parameter of IoCreateFileEx for more information about this parameter and for the list of flag values.

params.name: ObjectAttributes
params.description: Pointer to an opaque OBJECT_ATTRIBUTES structure that is already initialized with InitializeObjectAttributes. See the *ObjectAttributes* parameter of IoCreateFileEx for more information and for a description of each structure member.

params.name: IoStatusBlock
params.description: Pointer to an IO_STATUS_BLOCK structure that receives the final completion status and information about the requested operation. See the IoStatusBlock parameter of IoCreateFileEx.

params.name: AllocationSize
params.description: Optionally specifies the initial allocation size in bytes for the file. A nonzero value has no effect unless the file is being created, overwritten, or superseded.

params.name: FileAttributes
params.description: Explicitly specified attributes are applied only when the file is created, superseded, or, in some cases, overwritten. By default, this value is FILE_ATTRIBUTE_NORMAL, which can be overridden by an ORed combination of one or more FILE_ATTRIBUTE_*XXX* flags, which are defined in Wdm.h. For a list of flags that can be used with IoCreateFile, see CreateFile.

params.name: ShareAccess
params.description: Specifies the type of share access to the file that the caller requires, as zero or one, or a combination of the flags. See the *ShareAccess* parameter of IoCreateFileEx for more details and for the list of flags.

params.name: Disposition
params.description: Specifies a value that determines the action to be taken, depending on whether the file already exists. See the *Disposition* parameter of IoCreateFileEx for the list of possible values.

params.name: CreateOptions
params.description: Specifies the options to be applied when creating or opening the file. This parameter is a compatible combination of the flags listed and described in the *CreateOptions* parameter of IoCreateFileEx.

params.name: EaBuffer
params.description: For device and intermediate drivers, this parameter must be a NULL pointer.

params.name: EaLength
params.description: For device and intermediate drivers, this parameter must be zero.

params.name: CreateFileType
params.description: Drivers must set this parameter to CreateFileTypeNone.

params.name: InternalParameters
params.description: Drivers must set this parameter to NULL.

params.name: Options
params.description: Specifies options to be used during the creation of the create request. See the *Options* parameter of IoCreateFileEx for the list of possible options.

returns.description: IoCreateFile either returns STATUS_SUCCESS or an appropriate error status. NTSTATUS value. See the Return Value section of IoCreateFileEx for a list of possible return codes.

functions.name: IoCreateNotificationEvent
functions.summary: The IoCreateNotificationEvent function creates or opens a named notification event used to notify one or more threads of execution that an event has occurred.

params.name: EventName

params.name: EventHandle
params.description: Pointer to a location in which to return a kernel handle for the event object.

functions.summary: The IoCreateSynchronizationEvent function creates or opens a named synchronization event for use in serialization of access to hardware between two otherwise unrelated drivers.

params.description: Pointer to a location in which to return a handle for the event object. In Windows Server 2003 and later versions of Windows, the returned handle is a kernel handle.

functions.name: IoCreateSystemThread
functions.summary: The IoCreateSystemThread function creates a system thread that executes in kernel mode, and supplies a handle for the thread.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS IoCreateSystemThread(PVOID IoObject, PHANDLE ThreadHandle, ULONG DesiredAccess, POBJECT_ATTRIBUTES ObjectAttributes, HANDLE ProcessHandle, PCLIENT_ID ClientId, PKSTART_ROUTINE StartRoutine, PVOID StartContext);

params.name: IoObject
params.description: A pointer to the DEVICE_OBJECT or DRIVER_OBJECT to associate with the created thread. IoCreateSystemThread takes a counted reference to this object. The I/O manager later releases this reference when the thread exits. For more information, see Remarks.

params.name: ThreadHandle
params.description: A pointer to a variable to which the function writes the kernel handle for the created thread. When the handle is no longer needed, the driver must close the handle by calling the ZwClose function.

params.name: DesiredAccess
params.description: The ACCESS_MASK value that represents the types of access the caller requests to the created thread.

params.name: ObjectAttributes
params.description: A pointer to an OBJECT_ATTRIBUTES structure that specifies the thread object's attributes. The OBJ_PERMANENT, OBJ_EXCLUSIVE, and OBJ_OPENIF attributes are not valid attributes for a thread object. If the caller is not running in the system process context, it must set the OBJ_KERNEL_HANDLE attribute in the OBJECT_ATTRIBUTES structure.

params.name: ProcessHandle
params.description: An open handle for the process in whose address space the created thread is to run. The caller's thread must have PROCESS_CREATE_THREAD access to this process. If this parameter is NULL, the thread will be created in the initial system process. This parameter should be NULL for a driver-created thread. Use the NtCurrentProcess macro, defined in the Wdm.h header file, to specify the current process.

params.name: ClientId
params.description: A pointer to a structure to which the function writes the client identifier for the created thread. This parameter should be NULL for a driver-created thread.

params.name: StartRoutine
params.description: A pointer to a ThreadStart function that is the entry point for the created thread.

params.name: StartContext
params.description: A context pointer that is passed as the *StartContext* parameter to the ThreadStart function when the created thread starts to run.

returns.description: IoCreateSystemThread returns STATUS_SUCCESS if the new thread was successfully created. Possible return values include the following error status codes.

functions.name: IoCreateUnprotectedSymbolicLink
functions.summary: The IoCreateUnprotectedSymbolicLink function sets up an unprotected symbolic link between a device object name and a corresponding Win32-visible name.

params.name: SymbolicLinkName
params.description: Supplies the symbolic link name as a Unicode string.

params.name: DeviceName
params.description: Supplies the name of the device object to which the symbolic link name refers.

returns.description: IoCreateUnprotectedSymbolicLink returns the final status of the operation.

functions.name: IoCsqInsertIrp
functions.summary: The IoCsqInsertIrp function inserts an IRP in the driver's cancel-safe IRP queue.
functions.signature: void IoCsqInsertIrp(PIO_CSQ Csq, PIRP Irp, PIO_CSQ_IRP_CONTEXT Context);

params.name: Csq
params.description: Pointer to the IO_CSQ structure for the driver's cancel-safe IRP queue. This structure must have been initialized by IoCsqInitialize or IoCsqInitializeEx.

params.name: Irp
params.description: Pointer to the IRP to be queued.

params.name: Context
params.description: Pointer to an IO_CSQ_IRP_CONTEXT structure. IoCsqInsertIrp initializes this structure with context information for the inserted IRP. The driver passes this value to IoCsqRemoveIrp to delete the IRP from the queue. Context can be NULL if the driver will not use IoCsqRemoveIrp to remove this IRP from the queue.

returns.description: No value.

functions.name: IoCsqInsertIrpEx
functions.summary: The IoCsqInsertIrpEx function inserts an IRP into the driver's cancel-safe IRP queue.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS IoCsqInsertIrpEx(PIO_CSQ Csq, PIRP Irp, PIO_CSQ_IRP_CONTEXT Context, PVOID InsertContext);

params.name: Csq
params.description: Pointer to the IO_CSQ structure for the driver's cancel-safe IRP queue. This structure must have been initialized by IoCsqInitialize or IoCsqInitializeEx.

params.name: Irp
params.description: Pointer to the IRP to be queued.

params.name: Context
params.description: Pointer to an IO_CSQ_IRP_CONTEXT structure. IoCsqInsertIrpEx initializes this structure with context information for the inserted IRP. The driver passes this value to IoCsqRemoveIrp to delete the IRP from the queue. Context can be NULL if the driver will not use IoCsqRemoveIrp to remove this IRP from the queue.

params.name: InsertContext
params.description: Pointer to a driver-defined context value. This parameter is passed to the driver's CsqInsertIrpEx function, if it has one. Otherwise, this parameter is ignored.

returns.description: If the Csq parameter was initialized with IoCsqInitialize, IoCsqInsertIrpEx always returns STATUS_SUCCESS. If Csq was initialized with IoCsqInitializeEx, IoCsqInsertIrpEx returns the value that was returned by the driver's CsqInsertIrpEx function.

functions.name: IoCsqRemoveIrp
functions.summary: The IoCsqRemoveIrp function removes a particular IRP from the queue.

params.name: Context
params.description: Pointer to the IO_CSQ_IRP_CONTEXT structure that identifies the IRP to remove. The IO_CSQ_IRP_CONTEXT structure is initialized by IoCsqInsertIrp or IoCsqInsertIrpEx when the IRP is first inserted in the queue.

returns.description: This function returns a pointer to the IRP that was removed from the queue, or NULL if that IRP has been canceled.

functions.name: IoCsqRemoveNextIrp
functions.summary: The IoCsqRemoveNextIrp function removes the next matching IRP in the queue.

params.name: Csq

params.name: PeekContext
params.description: A pointer to a driver-defined context value. IoCsqRemoveNextIrp passes this parameter to the driver's CsqPeekNextIrp function. For more information, see the following Remarks section.

returns.description: This function returns a pointer to the next matching IRP in the queue, or NULL if no more IRPs are available. The function only returns IRPs that have not yet been canceled.

functions.name: IoRegisterContainerNotification
functions.summary: The IoRegisterContainerNotification function registers a kernel-mode driver to receive notifications about a specified class of events.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS IoRegisterContainerNotification(IO_CONTAINER_NOTIFICATION_CLASS NotificationClass, PIO_CONTAINER_NOTIFICATION_FUNCTION CallbackFunction, PVOID NotificationInformation, ULONG NotificationInformationLength, PVOID CallbackRegistration);

params.name: NotificationClass
params.description: Specifies the class of events for which the caller (driver) requests notifications. Set this parameter to the following IO_CONTAINER_NOTIFICATION_CLASS enumeration value:

params.name: CallbackFunction
params.description: A pointer to a callback function that is implemented by the caller (driver). The I/O manager calls this function to notify the caller when an event of the class indicated by *NotificationClass* occurs. For *NotificationClass* = IoSessionStateNotification, this parameter is a pointer to a caller-supplied IO_SESSION_NOTIFICATION_FUNCTION function. However, the caller should cast this function pointer to type PIO_CONTAINER_NOTIFICATION_FUNCTION to match the parameter type. For more information, see the following Remarks section.

params.name: NotificationInformation
params.description: A pointer to a caller-allocated buffer that contains the notification information structure for an event of the class specified by *NotificationClass*. For *NotificationClass* = IoSessionStateNotification, *NotificationInformation* points to an IO_SESSION_STATE_NOTIFICATION structure. The caller must fill out this structure before it calls IoRegisterContainerNotification. During this call, IoRegisterContainerNotification copies the data from this structure, and the I/O manager does not access the driver's copy of the structure after the call returns.

params.name: NotificationInformationLength
params.description: The size, in bytes, of the notification information structure contained in the buffer that is pointed to by *NotificationInformation*. For *NotificationClass* = IoSessionStateNotification, set this parameter to sizeof(IO_SESSION_STATE_NOTIFICATION).

params.name: CallbackRegistration
params.description: A pointer to a location into which this function writes the address of a container notification registration object. This object is an opaque, system object in which the I/O manager stores information about the caller's container notification registration. When notifications are no longer required, the caller cancels the registration by passing this object pointer to the IoUnregisterContainerNotification function.

returns.description: IoRegisterContainerNotification returns STATUS_SUCCESS if the call is successful. Possible error return values include the following:

params.description: Specifies whether the completion function is called if a driver or the kernel has called IoCancelIrp to cancel the IRP.

functions.name: KeAcquireGuardedMutexUnsafe
functions.summary: The KeAcquireGuardedMutexUnsafe acquires a guarded mutex while inside a guarded region.

returns.description: No value.

functions.name: KeAcquireInStackQueuedSpinLock
functions.summary: The KeAcquireInStackQueuedSpinLock function acquires a queued spin lock.

params.name: SpinLock
params.description: [in, out] Specifies the spin lock to acquire. This parameter must have been initialized with KeInitializeSpinLock.

params.name: LockHandle
params.description: [out] A pointer to a caller-supplied KLOCK_QUEUE_HANDLE variable that the function can use to return the spin lock queue handle. The caller passes this value to KeReleaseInStackQueuedSpinLock when releasing the lock. Drivers should normally allocate the structure on the stack each time they acquire the lock. A driver should not use the same KLOCK_QUEUE_HANDLE from multiple calling sites.

returns.description: No value.

functions.name: KeAcquireInStackQueuedSpinLockAtDpcLevel
functions.summary: The KeAcquireInStackQueuedSpinLockAtDpcLevel function acquires a queued spin lock when the caller is already running at IRQL \>= DISPATCH\_LEVEL.

params.name: SpinLock
params.description: [in, out] Specifies the spin lock to acquire. This parameter must have been initialized by a call to the KeInitializeSpinLock function.

params.name: LockHandle
params.description: [out] Pointer to a caller-supplied KLOCK\_QUEUE\_HANDLE structure that the function can use to return the spin lock queue handle. To release the lock, the caller passes this value to the KeReleaseInStackQueuedSpinLockFromDpcLevel function.

returns.description: No value.

functions.name: KeAcquireInStackQueuedSpinLockForDpc
functions.summary: The KeAcquireInStackQueuedSpinLockForDpc function acquires a queued spin lock for a threaded DPC.

params.name: SpinLock
params.description: [in, out] Pointer to the spin lock to acquire as a queued spin lock. You must have already initialized the spin lock by calling KeInitializeSpinLock.

params.name: LockHandle
params.description: [out] Pointer to a KLOCK\_QUEUE\_HANDLE structure that receives the lock queue handle. Pass this value to the KeReleaseInStackQueuedSpinLockForDpc function when you release the queued spin lock.

returns.description: No value.

functions.name: KeAcquireInterruptSpinLock
functions.summary: The KeAcquireInterruptSpinLock function acquires the spin lock associated with an interrupt object.

params.name: Interrupt
params.description: [in, out] Specifies a pointer to an interrupt object. This value must be supplied by IoConnectInterrupt or IoConnectInterruptEx.

returns.description: KeAcquireInterruptSpinLock returns the current IRQL at the time the function is called. This value is passed to KeReleaseInterruptSpinLock when the spin lock is released.

functions.name: KeAcquireSpinLockAtDpcLevel
functions.summary: The KeAcquireSpinLockAtDpcLevel function acquires a spin lock when the caller is already running at IRQL >= DISPATCH_LEVEL.

params.name: SpinLock
params.description: Pointer to an initialized KSPIN_LOCK spin lock for which the caller must provide the storage. The spin lock must be from non-paged pool.

returns.description: No value.

functions.name: KeAcquireSpinLockForDpc
functions.summary: The KeAcquireSpinLockForDpc function acquires a threaded DPC spin lock.

params.name: SpinLock
params.description: [in, out] Pointer to the spin lock to acquire. You must have already initialized the spin lock by calling KeInitializeSpinLock.

returns.description: KeAcquireSpinLockForDpc returns the current IRQL at the time the function is called. Pass this value to KeReleaseSpinLockForDpc when you release the spin lock.

functions.name: KeAcquireSpinLockRaiseToDpc
functions.summary: The KeAcquireSpinLockRaiseToDpc function is a faster version of the KeAcquireSpinLock function.

params.name: SpinLock
params.description: [in, out] Specifies the spin lock to acquire. The spin lock must already have been initialized by KeInitializeSpinLock.

returns.description: KeAcquireSpinLockRaiseToDpc returns the current IRQL at the time the function is called. This value is passed to KeReleaseSpinLock) when the spin lock is released.

functions.name: KeAddTriageDumpDataBlock
functions.summary: Adds a triage dump data block to a triage dump data block array.

params.name: KtriageDumpDataArray

params.name: Size

functions.name: KeAreAllApcsDisabled
functions.summary: The KeAreAllApcsDisabled function indicates whether the calling thread is inside a guarded region or running at IRQL >= APC_LEVEL, which disables all APC delivery.

returns.description: KeAreAllApcsDisabled returns TRUE if the calling thread is inside a guarded region or running at IRQL >= APC_LEVEL, and FALSE otherwise.

functions.name: KeAreApcsDisabled
functions.summary: The KeAreApcsDisabled function returns whether the calling thread is within a critical region or a guarded region, which disables normal kernel APC delivery.

returns.description: KeAreApcsDisabled returns TRUE if the thread is within a critical region or a guarded region, and FALSE otherwise.

functions.name: KeBugCheckEx
functions.summary: The KeBugCheckEx function brings down the system in a controlled manner when the caller discovers an unrecoverable inconsistency that would corrupt the system if the caller continued to run.
functions.signature: void KeBugCheckEx(ULONG BugCheckCode, ULONG_PTR BugCheckParameter1, ULONG_PTR BugCheckParameter2, ULONG_PTR BugCheckParameter3, ULONG_PTR BugCheckParameter4);

params.name: BugCheckParameter3

params.name: BugCheckParameter4
params.description: The four BugCheckParameterX values supply additional information, such as the address and data where a memory-corruption error occurred, depending on the value of BugCheckCode.

functions.name: KeCancelTimer
functions.summary: The KeCancelTimer function dequeues a timer object before the timer interval, if any was set, expires.

params.name: Event

returns.description: No value.

params.name: AuxiliaryCounterValue
params.description: A pointer to the variable that contains the converted auxiliary counter value.

functions.name: KeDelayExecutionThread
functions.summary: The KeDelayExecutionThread function puts the current thread into an alertable or nonalertable wait state for a specified interval.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS KeDelayExecutionThread(KPROCESSOR_MODE WaitMode, BOOLEAN Alertable, PLARGE_INTEGER Interval);

params.name: WaitMode
params.description: Specifies the processor mode in which the caller is waiting, which can be either KernelMode or UserMode. Lower-level drivers should specify KernelMode.

params.name: Alertable
params.description: Specifies TRUE if the wait is alertable. Lower-level drivers should specify FALSE.

params.name: Interval
params.description: Specifies the absolute or relative time, in units of 100 nanoseconds, for which the wait is to occur. A negative value indicates relative time. Absolute expiration times track any changes in system time; relative expiration times are not affected by system time changes.

returns.description: KeDelayExecutionThread returns one of the following values that describes how the delay was completed:

functions.name: KeDeregisterBoundCallback
functions.summary: The KeDeregisterBoundCallback function deregisters a user-mode bound exception callback registered by KeRegisterBoundCallback.

params.name: Handle
params.description: Specifies the value returned by KeRegisterBoundCallback when the callback was registered.

returns.description: The KeDeregisterBoundCallback function returns STATUS_SUCCESS if the callback is successfully removed. It returns STATUS_INVALID_HANDLE if no callback matching the provided Handle value is found.

functions.name: KeDeregisterBugCheckCallback
functions.summary: The KeDeregisterBugCheckCallback function removes a callback function that was registered by KeRegisterBugCheckCallback.

params.name: CallbackRecord
params.description: Pointer to a KBUGCHECK_CALLBACK_RECORD structure. CallbackRecord must be the same value that was passed to KeRegisterBugCheckCallback when the callback was registered.

returns.description: KeDeregisterBugCheckCallback returns TRUE if the specified callback is successfully removed. It returns FALSE if the specified callback is not registered.

functions.name: KeDeregisterBugCheckReasonCallback
functions.summary: The KeDeregisterBugCheckReasonCallback function removes a callback function that was registered by KeRegisterBugCheckReasonCallback.

params.name: CallbackRecord
params.description: Pointer to a KBUGCHECK_REASON_CALLBACK_RECORD structure. CallbackRecord must be the same value that was passed to KeRegisterBugCheckReasonCallback when the callback was registered.

returns.description: KeDeregisterBugCheckReasonCallback returns TRUE if the callback is successfully removed. It returns FALSE if the specified callback is not registered.

functions.name: KeDeregisterNmiCallback
functions.summary: The KeDeregisterNmiCallback function deregisters a nonmaskable interrupt (NMI) callback registered by KeRegisterNmiCallback.

params.name: Handle
params.description: Specifies the value returned by KeRegisterNmiCallback when the NMI callback was registered.

returns.description: The KeDeregisterNmiCallback function returns STATUS_SUCCESS if the callback is successfully removed. It returns STATUS_INVALID_HANDLE if no callback matching the provided Handle value is found.

functions.name: KeDeregisterProcessorChangeCallback
functions.summary: The KeDeregisterProcessorChangeCallback function unregisters a callback function that was previously registered with the operating system by calling the KeRegisterProcessorChangeCallback function.

params.name: CallbackHandle
params.description: The callback registration handle that was returned by the KeRegisterProcessorChangeCallback function when the callback function was registered with the operating system.

returns.description: No value.

functions.name: KeEnterCriticalRegion
functions.summary: The KeEnterCriticalRegion function temporarily disables the execution of normal kernel APCs, but does not prevent special kernel APCs from running.

returns.description: No value.

functions.name: KeEnterGuardedRegion
functions.summary: The KeEnterGuardedRegion function enters a guarded region, which disables all kernel-mode APC delivery to the current thread.

returns.description: No value.

functions.name: KeFlushIoBuffers
functions.summary: The KeFlushIoBuffers function flushes the memory region described by an MDL from caches of all processors.
functions.signature: void KeFlushIoBuffers(PMDL Mdl, BOOLEAN ReadOperation, BOOLEAN DmaOperation);

params.name: Mdl
params.description: A pointer to an MDL that describes the range for the I/O buffer.

params.name: ReadOperation
params.description: Specifies TRUE if the flush is being performed for a read operation, and FALSE for a write operation. For more information, see the following Remarks section.

params.name: DmaOperation
params.description: Specifies TRUE for a DMA transfer, FALSE for PIO.

returns.description: No value.

functions.name: KeFlushQueuedDpcs
functions.summary: The KeFlushQueuedDpcs function returns after all currently queued DPCs on all processors have executed their DPC functions to completion.

returns.description: No value.

functions.name: KeGetCurrentIrql
functions.summary: The KeGetCurrentIrql function returns the current IRQL. For information about IRQLs, see Managing Hardware Priorities.

returns.description: KeGetCurrentIrql returns the current IRQL.

functions.name: KeGetCurrentNodeNumber
functions.summary: The KeGetCurrentNodeNumber function gets the NUMA node number for the logical processor that the caller is running on.

returns.description: KeGetCurrentNodeNumber returns the node number.

functions.name: KeGetCurrentProcessorIndex
functions.summary: KeGetCurrentProcessorIndex returns the index of the processor that the caller is running on.

returns.description: KeGetCurrentProcessorIndex returns the system wide index of the logical processor the caller is running on.

functions.name: KeGetCurrentProcessorNumberEx
functions.summary: The KeGetCurrentProcessorNumberEx function gets the processor number of the logical processor that the caller is running on.

params.name: ProcNumber
params.description: A pointer to a caller-allocated buffer into which the function writes a PROCESSOR_NUMBER structure that identifies the current logical processor. This structure contains the group number and the group-relative processor number. You can set this parameter to NULL if you do not need this information.

returns.description: KeGetCurrentProcessorNumberEx returns the systemwide processor index of the logical processor that the caller is running on.

functions.name: KeGetCurrentThread
functions.summary: The KeGetCurrentThread function identifies the current thread.

returns.description: KeGetCurrentThread returns a pointer to an opaque thread object.

functions.name: KeGetProcessorIndexFromNumber
functions.summary: The KeGetProcessorIndexFromNumber function converts a group number and a group-relative processor number to a systemwide processor index.

params.name: ProcNumber
params.description: A pointer to a caller-allocated PROCESSOR_NUMBER structure that contains a group number and a group-relative processor number.

returns.description: KeGetProcessorIndexFromNumber returns a systemwide processor index if the call is successful. If ProcNumber points to an invalid PROCESSOR_NUMBER value, the function returns INVALID_PROCESSOR_INDEX, which is defined in the Wdm.h header file.

functions.name: KeGetProcessorNumberFromIndex
functions.summary: The KeGetProcessorNumberFromIndex function converts a systemwide processor index to a group number and a group-relative processor number.

params.name: ProcIndex
params.description: A systemwide processor index. If a multiprocessor system contains a total of *n* logical processors, valid processor indexes range from 0 to *n*-1.

params.name: ProcNumber
params.description: A pointer to a caller-allocated PROCESSOR_NUMBER structure into which the function writes the group number and group-relative processor number of the processor that is identified by *ProcIndex*.

returns.description: KeGetProcessorNumberFromIndex returns STATUS_SUCCESS if the call is successful. Possible error return values include the following:

functions.name: KeGetRecommendedSharedDataAlignment
functions.summary: The KeGetRecommendedSharedDataAlignment function returns the preferred alignment for memory structures that can be accessed by more than one processor.

returns.description: KeGetRecommendedSharedDataAlignment returns the preferred alignment, in bytes, for memory structures that can be shared by more than one processor.

functions.name: KeInitializeCrashDumpHeader
functions.summary: The KeInitializeCrashDumpHeader function supplies the header information the system requires for a crash dump file.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS KeInitializeCrashDumpHeader(ULONG DumpType, ULONG Flags, PVOID Buffer, ULONG BufferSize, PULONG BufferNeeded);

params.name: DumpType
params.description: Specifies the type of dump file. The only valid value is DUMP_TYPE_FULL.

params.name: Flags
params.description: Specifies flags for the dump file. The only valid value is 0.

params.name: Buffer
params.description: Pointer to the buffer that receives the header information.

params.name: BufferSize
params.description: Specifies the size in bytes of the buffer pointed to by Buffer.

params.name: BufferNeeded
params.description: Optionally, a pointer to a variable that receives the size necessary to hold the complete header information.

returns.description: KeInitializeCrashDumpHeader returns STATUS_SUCCESS on success, or the appropriate NTSTATUS error code on failure.

functions.name: KeInitializeDeviceQueue
functions.summary: The KeInitializeDeviceQueue function initializes a device queue object to a not-busy state.

returns.description: No value.

functions.name: KeInitializeDpc

params.description: Specifies the value to pass as the DeferredContext parameter to CustomDpc.

params.name: Event
params.description: Pointer to an event object, for which the caller provides the storage.

params.name: Type
params.description: Specifies the event type, either NotificationEvent or SynchronizationEvent.

params.name: State
params.description: Specifies the initial state of the event. TRUE indicates a signaled state.

returns.description: No value.

functions.name: KeInitializeGuardedMutex
functions.summary: The KeInitializeGuardedMutex function initializes a guarded mutex.

params.name: Mutex
params.description: Pointer to the KGUARDED_MUTEX structure to initialize. The storage must be 4-byte aligned on 32-bit platforms, and 8-byte aligned on 64-bit platforms.

returns.description: No value.

functions.name: KeInitializeMutex
functions.summary: The KeInitializeMutex function initializes a mutex object, setting it to a signaled state.

params.name: Mutex
params.description: Pointer to a mutex object, for which the caller provides the storage. The storage must be 4-byte aligned on 32-bit platforms, and 8-byte aligned on 64-bit platforms.

params.name: Level
params.description: Reserved. Drivers set this to zero.

returns.description: No value.

functions.name: KeInitializeSemaphore
functions.summary: The KeInitializeSemaphore function initializes a semaphore object with a specified count and specifies an upper limit that the count can attain.
functions.signature: void KeInitializeSemaphore(PRKSEMAPHORE Semaphore, LONG Count, LONG Limit);

params.name: Semaphore
params.description: Pointer to a dispatcher object of type semaphore, for which the caller provides the storage.

params.name: Count
params.description: Specifies the initial count value to be assigned to the semaphore. This value must be positive. A nonzero value sets the initial state of the semaphore to signaled.

params.name: Limit
params.description: Specifies the maximum count value that the semaphore can attain. This value must be positive. It determines how many waiting threads become eligible for execution when the semaphore is set to the signaled state and can therefore access the resource that the semaphore protects.

returns.description: No value.

functions.name: KeInitializeSpinLock
functions.summary: The KeInitializeSpinLock function initializes a variable of type KSPIN_LOCK.

params.name: SpinLock
params.description: Pointer to a spin lock, for which the caller must provide the storage.

returns.description: No value.

functions.name: KeInitializeThreadedDpc
functions.summary: The KeInitializeThreadedDpc function initializes a threaded DPC object, and registers a CustomThreadedDpc function for that object.
functions.signature: void KeInitializeThreadedDpc(PRKDPC Dpc, PKDEFERRED_ROUTINE DeferredRoutine, PVOID DeferredContext);

params.name: Dpc
params.description: Pointer to a KDPC structure that represents the DPC object to initialize. The caller must allocate storage for the structure from resident memory.

params.description: Pointer to the *CustomThreadedDpc* function to associate with the DPC.

params.name: DeferredContext
params.description: Specifies the value to pass as the *DeferredContext* parameter to *CustomThreadedDpc*.

returns.description: No value.

functions.name: KeInitializeTimer
functions.summary: The KeInitializeTimer function initializes a timer object.

params.name: Timer
params.description: Pointer to a timer object, for which the caller provides the storage.

returns.description: No value.

functions.name: KeInitializeTimerEx

params.name: Type
params.description: Specifies the type of the timer object, either NotificationTimer or SynchronizationTimer.

returns.description: No value.

params.description: Specifies the size, in bytes, of the uninitialized triage dump data array.

params.description: Pointer to a control object of type device queue for which the caller provides the storage.

params.name: DeviceQueueEntry
params.description: Pointer to the device queue entry that is to be inserted.

returns.description: If the device queue is empty, FALSE is returned and the DeviceQueueEntry is not inserted in the device queue.

functions.name: KeInsertQueueDpc

params.description: Specifies driver-determined context data. This value is passed as the *SystemArgument1* parameter to the DPC object's CustomDpc or CustomThreadedDpc function.

functions.name: KeLeaveCriticalRegion

functions.summary: The KeLeaveGuardedRegion function exits a guarded region entered by KeEnterGuardedRegion.

functions.name: KeQueryActiveGroupCount

functions.summary: The KeQueryActiveProcessorCount function returns the number of currently active processors.

params.description: A pointer to a KAFFINITY-typed variable into which the function writes a bitmask that represents the set of currently active processors. In a hot-add environment, this mask may change during runtime. This parameter is optional and can be specified as NULL if the caller does not require the mask of active processors.

returns.description: KeQueryActiveProcessorCount returns the number of currently active processors.
