functions.summary: The KeQueryActiveProcessorCountEx function returns the number of active logical processors in a specified group in a multiprocessor system or in the entire system.

params.description: The group number. If a multiprocessor system contains n groups, valid group numbers range from 0 to n-1. To count all active processors in all groups in the system, set this parameter to ALL_PROCESSOR_GROUPS, which is defined in header files Winnt.h and Ntdef.h.

returns.description: KeQueryActiveProcessorCountEx returns the number of active logical processors in the group. If GroupNumber is not a valid group number and is not ALL_PROCESSOR_GROUPS, it returns zero.

functions.name: KeQueryActiveProcessors

returns.description: KeQueryAuxiliaryCounterFrequency can return one of the following:

params.description: The group number. If a multiprocessor system contains n groups, the groups are numbered from 0 to n-1. To obtain the number of active groups in the system, call the KeQueryActiveGroupCount function.

returns.description: KeQueryGroupAffinity returns a KAFFINITY value that identifies the active logical processors in the specified group. If the GroupNumber parameter value is not a valid group number, the function returns zero.

You can set this parameter to NULL if you do not need this information.

functions.name: KeSetCoalescableTimer
functions.summary: The KeSetCoalescableTimer function sets the initial expiration time and period of a timer object and specifies how much delay can be tolerated in the expiration times.
functions.signature: BOOLEAN KeSetCoalescableTimer(PKTIMER Timer, LARGE_INTEGER DueTime, ULONG Period, ULONG TolerableDelay, PKDPC Dpc);

params.name: Timer
params.description: A pointer to a timer object. This parameter points to a KTIMER structure, which is an opaque, system structure that represents the timer object. This object must have been previously initialized by the KeInitializeTimerEx or KeInitializeTimer function.

params.name: DueTime
params.description: Specifies an absolute or relative time at which the timer is to expire. If the value of the *DueTime* parameter is negative, the expiration time is relative to the current system time. Otherwise, the expiration time is absolute. The expiration time is expressed in system time units, which are 100-nanosecond intervals. Absolute expiration times track any changes that are made to the system clock. Relative expiration times are not affected by system clock changes.

params.name: Period
params.description: Specifies the interval between periodic timer expirations in milliseconds. The value of this parameter must not exceed MAXLONG. This parameter is optional and can be set to zero to indicate that the timer is nonperiodic.

params.name: TolerableDelay
params.description: Specifies a tolerance, in milliseconds, for the timer period that *Period* specifies and for the initial time interval that *DueTime* specifies. For a periodic timer, the time interval between two successive timer expirations will be in the range from (*Period* - *TolerableDelay*) to (*Period* + *TolerableDelay*). The initial expiration time will be in the range from *DueTime* to (*DueTime* + *TolerableDelay*). The *TolerableDelay* value cannot be negative.

params.name: Dpc
params.description: A pointer to a DPC object. This parameter points to a KDPC structure, which is an opaque, system structure that represents the DPC object. This object must have been previously initialized by the KeInitializeDpc function. This parameter is optional and can be specified as NULL if the caller does not require a DPC.

returns.description: KeSetCoalescableTimer returns TRUE if the timer object was already in the system timer queue. Otherwise, it returns FALSE.

functions.name: KeSetTimer
functions.summary: The KeSetTimer function sets the absolute or relative interval at which a timer object is to be set to a signaled state and, optionally, supplies a CustomTimerDpc function to be executed when that interval expires.
functions.signature: BOOLEAN KeSetTimer(PKTIMER Timer, LARGE_INTEGER DueTime, PKDPC Dpc);

params.name: Timer
params.description: Pointer to a timer object that was initialized with KeInitializeTimer or KeInitializeTimerEx.

params.name: DueTime
params.description: Specifies the absolute or relative time at which the timer is to expire. If the value of the *DueTime* parameter is negative, the expiration time is relative to the current system time. Otherwise, the expiration time is absolute. The expiration time is expressed in system time units (100-nanosecond intervals). Absolute expiration times track any changes in the system time; relative expiration times are not affected by system time changes.

params.name: Dpc
params.description: Pointer to a DPC object that was initialized by KeInitializeDpc. This parameter is optional.

returns.description: If the timer object was already in the system timer queue, KeSetTimer returns TRUE.

functions.name: KeSetTimerEx
functions.summary: The KeSetTimerEx function sets the absolute or relative interval at which a timer object is to be set to a signaled state, optionally supplies a CustomTimerDpc function to be executed when that interval expires, and optionally supplies a recurring interval for the timer.
functions.signature: BOOLEAN KeSetTimerEx(PKTIMER Timer, LARGE_INTEGER DueTime, LONG Period, PKDPC Dpc);

params.name: Timer
params.description: Pointer to a timer object that was initialized with KeInitializeTimer or KeInitializeTimerEx.

params.name: DueTime
params.description: Specifies the absolute or relative time at which the timer is to expire. If the value of the *DueTime* parameter is negative, the expiration time is relative to the current system time. Otherwise, the expiration time is absolute. The expiration time is expressed in system time units (100-nanosecond intervals). Absolute expiration times track any changes in the system time; relative expiration times are not affected by system time changes.

params.name: Period
params.description: Specifies an optional recurring interval for the timer in milliseconds. Must be a value that is greater than or equal to zero. If the value of this parameter is zero, the timer is a nonperiodic timer that does not automatically re-queue itself.

params.name: Dpc
params.description: Pointer to a DPC object that was initialized by KeInitializeDpc. This parameter is optional.

returns.description: If the timer object was already in the system timer queue, KeSetTimerEx returns TRUE.

functions.name: KeWaitForMultipleObjects
functions.summary: The KeWaitForMultipleObjects function puts the current thread into an alertable or nonalertable wait state until any or all of a number of dispatcher objects are set to a signaled state or (optionally) until the wait times out.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS KeWaitForMultipleObjects(ULONG Count, PVOID * Object, WAIT_TYPE WaitType, KWAIT_REASON WaitReason, KPROCESSOR_MODE WaitMode, BOOLEAN Alertable, PLARGE_INTEGER Timeout, PKWAIT_BLOCK WaitBlockArray);

params.name: Count
params.description: The number of objects to be waited on. This parameter specifies the number of elements in the array pointed to by the *Object* parameter.

params.name: Object
params.description: A pointer to an array of pointers to dispatcher objects (events, mutexes, semaphores, threads, and timers) for which the caller supplies the storage. Both the pointer array and the dispatcher objects must reside in nonpaged system memory. For more information, see Remarks.

params.name: WaitType
params.description: The type of wait operation to perform. Specify either WaitAll, indicating that all of the specified objects must attain a signaled state before the wait is satisfied; or WaitAny, indicating that any one of the objects must attain a signaled state before the wait is satisfied.

params.name: WaitReason
params.description: The reason for the wait. Drivers should set this value to Executive or, if the driver is doing work on behalf of a user and is running in the context of a user thread, to UserRequest.

params.name: WaitMode
params.description: Whether the caller waits in KernelMode or UserMode. Intermediate and lowest-level drivers should specify KernelMode. If the set of objects waited on includes a mutex, the caller must specify KernelMode.

params.name: Alertable
params.description: A Boolean value that indicates whether the thread can be alerted while it is in the waiting state.

params.name: Timeout
params.description: A pointer to a time-out value that specifies the absolute or relative time, in 100-nanosecond units, at which the wait is to be completed.

params.name: WaitBlockArray
params.description: A pointer to a caller-allocated KWAIT_BLOCK array. If *Count* <= THREAD_WAIT_OBJECTS, then *WaitBlockArray* can be NULL. Otherwise, this parameter must point to a memory buffer of sizeof(KWAIT_BLOCK) \* *Count* bytes. The function uses this buffer for record-keeping while performing the wait operation. The *WaitBlockArray* buffer must reside in nonpaged system memory. For more information, see Remarks.

returns.description: KeWaitForMultipleObjects can return one of the following:

functions.name: KeWaitForSingleObject
functions.summary: The KeWaitForSingleObject function puts the current thread into a wait state until the given dispatcher object is set to a signaled state or (optionally) until the wait times out.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS KeWaitForSingleObject(PVOID Object, KWAIT_REASON WaitReason, KPROCESSOR_MODE WaitMode, BOOLEAN Alertable, PLARGE_INTEGER Timeout);

params.name: Object
params.description: Pointer to an initialized dispatcher object (event, mutex, semaphore, thread, or timer) for which the caller supplies the storage. The dispatcher object must reside in nonpaged system memory. For more information, see Remarks.

params.name: WaitReason
params.description: Specifies the reason for the wait. A driver should set this value to Executive, unless it is doing work on behalf of a user and is running in the context of a user thread, in which case it should set this value to UserRequest.

params.name: WaitMode
params.description: Specifies whether the caller waits in KernelMode or UserMode. Lowest-level and intermediate drivers should specify KernelMode. If the given *Object* is a mutex, the caller must specify KernelMode.

params.name: Alertable
params.description: Specifies a Boolean value that is TRUE if the wait is alertable and FALSE otherwise.

params.name: Timeout
params.description: Pointer to a time-out value that specifies the absolute or relative time, in 100-nanosecond units, at which the wait is to be completed.

returns.description: KeWaitForSingleObject can return one of the following.

functions.name: MmAllocateContiguousMemory
functions.summary: The MmAllocateContiguousMemory function allocates a range of contiguous, nonpaged physical memory and maps it to the system address space.

params.name: NumberOfBytes
params.description: The size, in bytes, of the block of contiguous memory to allocate. For more information, see Remarks.

params.name: HighestAcceptableAddress
params.description: The highest valid physical address the caller can use. For example, if a device can address only locations in the first 16 megabytes of the processor's physical memory address range, the driver for this device should set *HighestAcceptableAddress* to 0x0000000000FFFFFF. If you do not have specific requirements for memory allocation, set to MAXULONG64.

returns.description: MmAllocateContiguousMemory returns the base virtual address for the allocated memory. If the request cannot be satisfied, the function returns NULL.

functions.name: MmAllocateContiguousMemoryEx
functions.summary: The MmAllocateContiguousMemoryEx function allocates a range of physically contiguous non-paged memory and returns its virtual address.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS MmAllocateContiguousMemoryEx(PSIZE_T NumberOfBytes, PHYSICAL_ADDRESS LowestAcceptableAddress, PHYSICAL_ADDRESS HighestAcceptableAddress, PHYSICAL_ADDRESS BoundaryAddressMultiple, NODE_REQUIREMENT PreferredNode, ULONG Protect, PVOID PartitionObject, ULONG Tag, ULONG Flags, PVOID * BaseAddress);

params.name: NumberOfBytes
params.description: On entry, supplies the number of bytes to allocate. On successful return, receives the amount allocated.

params.name: LowestAcceptableAddress
params.description: Supplies the lowest physical address which is valid for the allocation. For example, if the device can only reference physical memory in the 8M to 16MB range, this value would be set to 0x800000 (8Mb).

params.name: HighestAcceptableAddress
params.description: Supplies the highest physical address which is valid for the allocation. For example, if the device can only reference physical memory below 16MB, this value would be set to 0xFFFFFF (16Mb - 1).

params.name: BoundaryAddressMultiple
params.description: Supplies the physical address multiple this allocation must not cross.

params.name: PreferredNode
params.description: Supplies the preferred node the allocation should be made from if pages are available on that node. MM_ANY_NODE_OK is used to signify no node preference.

params.name: Protect
params.description: Supplies the desired protection (including cache type) for the mapping.

params.name: PartitionObject
params.description: If specified, supplies a partition object to allocate the physical memory from. If not specified, the memory will come from the system partition.

params.name: Tag
params.description: Supplies the tag for the allocation.

params.name: Flags
params.description: Various flags:

params.name: BaseAddress
params.description: On success, receives the base virtual address of the contiguous memory.

returns.description: Returns an NTSTATUS code.

functions.name: MmAllocateContiguousMemorySpecifyCache
functions.summary: The MmAllocateContiguousMemorySpecifyCache function allocates a range of contiguous, nonpaged physical memory and maps it to the system address space.
functions.signature: PVOID MmAllocateContiguousMemorySpecifyCache(SIZE_T NumberOfBytes, PHYSICAL_ADDRESS LowestAcceptableAddress, PHYSICAL_ADDRESS HighestAcceptableAddress, PHYSICAL_ADDRESS BoundaryAddressMultiple, MEMORY_CACHING_TYPE CacheType);

params.name: NumberOfBytes
params.description: The size, in bytes, of the block of contiguous memory to allocate. For more information, see Remarks.

params.name: LowestAcceptableAddress
params.description: The lowest valid physical address the caller can use. For example, if a device can address only locations above the first 8 megabytes of the processor's physical memory address range, the driver for this device should set *LowestAcceptableAddress* to 0x0000000000800000.

params.name: HighestAcceptableAddress
params.description: The highest valid physical address the caller can use. For example, if a device can address only locations in the first 16 megabytes of the processor's physical memory address range, the driver for this device should set *HighestAcceptableAddress* to 0x0000000000FFFFFF.

params.name: BoundaryAddressMultiple
params.description: The physical address multiple that the allocated buffer must not cross. A physical address multiple must always be a power of two. This parameter is optional and can be specified as zero to indicate that the device has no special memory boundary restrictions. For more information, see Remarks.

params.name: CacheType
params.description: Specifies a MEMORY_CACHING_TYPE value, which indicates the type of caching allowed for the requested memory.

returns.description: MmAllocateContiguousMemorySpecifyCache returns the base virtual address for the allocated memory. If the system is unable to allocate the requested buffer, the function returns NULL.

functions.name: MmAllocateContiguousMemorySpecifyCacheNode
functions.summary: The MmAllocateContiguousMemorySpecifyCacheNode function allocates a range of contiguous, nonpaged physical memory and maps it to the system address space.
functions.signature: PVOID MmAllocateContiguousMemorySpecifyCacheNode(SIZE_T NumberOfBytes, PHYSICAL_ADDRESS LowestAcceptableAddress, PHYSICAL_ADDRESS HighestAcceptableAddress, PHYSICAL_ADDRESS BoundaryAddressMultiple, MEMORY_CACHING_TYPE CacheType, NODE_REQUIREMENT PreferredNode);

params.name: NumberOfBytes
params.description: The size, in bytes, of the block of contiguous memory to allocate. For more information, see the Remarks section below.

params.name: LowestAcceptableAddress
params.description: The lowest valid physical address the caller can use. For example, if a device can address only locations above the first 8 megabytes of the processor's physical memory address range, the driver for this device should set *LowestAcceptableAddress* to 0x0000000000800000.

params.name: HighestAcceptableAddress
params.description: The highest valid physical address the caller can use. For example, if a device can address only locations in the first 16 megabytes of the processor's physical memory address range, the driver for this device should set *HighestAcceptableAddress* to 0x0000000000FFFFFF.

params.name: BoundaryAddressMultiple
params.description: The physical address multiple that the allocated buffer must not cross. A physical address multiple must always be a power of two. This parameter is optional and can be specified as zero to indicate that the device has no special memory boundary restrictions. For more information, see Remarks.

params.name: CacheType
params.description: Specifies a MEMORY_CACHING_TYPE value, which indicates the type of caching requested for the contiguous physical memory.

params.name: PreferredNode
params.description: The preferred node number. If a multiprocessor system contains N nodes, the nodes are numbered 0 to N-1. If MM_ANY_NODE_OK is specified or the machine only has one node, then the allocation is satisfied from any node. Otherwise, the allocation is made from the preferred node or if a satisfactory range cannot be found from the preferred node, then NULL is returned.

If insufficient memory is available in the ideal node to satisfy the allocation request, and the caller does not set the MM_ALLOCATE_FROM_LOCAL_NODE_ONLY flag, MmAllocateNodePagesForMdlEx will try to allocate memory from other nodes.

params.name: MemoryDescriptorList
params.description: Pointer to an MDL that was updated by MmProbeAndLockPages.

functions.name: MmMapLockedPagesSpecifyCache
functions.summary: The MmMapLockedPagesSpecifyCache function maps the physical pages that are described by an MDL to a virtual address, and enables the caller to specify the cache attribute that is used to create the mapping.
functions.signature: PVOID MmMapLockedPagesSpecifyCache(PMDL MemoryDescriptorList, KPROCESSOR_MODE AccessMode, MEMORY_CACHING_TYPE CacheType, PVOID RequestedAddress, ULONG BugCheckOnFailure, ULONG Priority);

params.name: MemoryDescriptorList
params.description: A pointer to the MDL that is to be mapped. This MDL must describe physical pages that are locked down. A locked-down MDL can be built by the MmProbeAndLockPages or MmAllocatePagesForMdlEx function. For mappings to user space, MDLs that are built by the MmBuildMdlForNonPagedPool function can be used.

params.name: AccessMode
params.description: Specifies the access mode in which to map the MDL: KernelMode or UserMode. Almost all drivers should use KernelMode.

params.name: CacheType
params.description: Specifies a MEMORY_CACHING_TYPE value, which indicates the cache attribute to use to map the MDL. For more information, see the following Remarks section.

params.name: RequestedAddress
params.description: If *AccessMode* = UserMode, this parameter specifies the starting user virtual address to map the MDL to, or set to NULL to allow the system to choose the starting address. The system might round down the requested address to fit address boundary requirements, so callers must check the return value.

params.name: BugCheckOnFailure
params.description: Specifies the behavior of the function for *AccessMode* = KernelMode if the MDL cannot be mapped because of low system resources. If TRUE, the system issues a bug check. If FALSE, the function returns NULL. Drivers must set this parameter to FALSE.

params.name: Priority
params.description: An MM_PAGE_PRIORITY value that indicates the importance of success when page table entries (PTEs) are scarce. Starting with Windows 8, the specified priority value can be bitwise-ORed with the MdlMappingNoWrite or MdlMappingNoExecute flags to specify memory in which writes or instruction execution are disabled. For more information about the possible values for *Priority*, see MmGetSystemAddressForMdlSafe.

returns.description: MmMapLockedPagesSpecifyCache returns the starting address of the mapped pages. If the pages cannot be mapped and *BugCheckOnFailure* is FALSE, the function returns NULL.

lines: _In_     ULONG Priority  // MM_PAGE_PRIORITY logically OR'd with MdlMapping*

params.description: Specifies the MEMORY_CACHING_TYPE value to use to create the mapping.

This function returns NULL only if there is an error in the function parameters (for example, the driver's mapping address is not large enough to span the supplied MDL). IoWriteAccess and IoModifyAccess, which are equivalent, indicate that the driver has both read and write access to the buffer.

The resource manager receives this pointer when it calls ZwGetNotificationResourceManager or when KTM calls the ResourceManagerNotification callback function. The resource manager can maintain a reference count for this key by calling TmReferenceEnlistmentKey and TmDereferenceEnlistmentKey. This parameter is optional and can be NULL.

returns.description: ZwCreateEnlistment returns STATUS_SUCCESS if the operation succeeds. Otherwise, this function might return one of the following values:

params.name: ResourceManagerHandle
params.description: A pointer to a caller-allocated variable that receives a handle to the new resource manager object if the call to ZwCreateResourceManager is successful.

params.name: DesiredAccess
params.description: An ACCESS_MASK value that specifies the caller's requested access to the resource manager object. In addition to the access rights that are defined for all kinds of objects (see ACCESS_MASK), the caller can specify any of the following access right flags for resource manager objects:

If the caller is not running in a system thread context, it must set the OBJ_KERNEL_HANDLE attribute when it calls InitializeObjectAttributes. This parameter is optional and can be NULL.

params.name: CreateOptions
params.description: Optional object creation flags. The following table contains the available flags, which are defined in Ktmtypes.h.

KTM stores a copy of the string and includes the string in messages that it writes to the log stream. The maximum string length is MAX_RESOURCEMANAGER_DESCRIPTION_LENGTH. returns.description: ZwCreateResourceManager returns STATUS_SUCCESS if the operation succeeds. Otherwise, this function might return one of the following values:

functions.name: NtCreateTransaction
functions.summary: The ZwCreateTransaction function creates a transaction object.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS NtCreateTransaction(PHANDLE TransactionHandle, ACCESS_MASK DesiredAccess, POBJECT_ATTRIBUTES ObjectAttributes, LPGUID Uow, HANDLE TmHandle, ULONG CreateOptions, ULONG IsolationLevel, ULONG IsolationFlags, PLARGE_INTEGER Timeout, PUNICODE_STRING Description);

params.name: TransactionHandle
params.description: A pointer to a caller-allocated variable that receives a handle to the new transaction object, if the call to ZwCreateTransaction succeeds.

params.name: DesiredAccess
params.description: An ACCESS_MASK value that specifies the caller's requested access to the transaction object. In addition to the access rights that are defined for all kinds of objects (see ACCESS_MASK), the caller can specify any of the following flags for transaction objects.

params.name: ObjectAttributes
params.description: A pointer to an OBJECT_ATTRIBUTES structure that specifies the object name and other attributes. Use the InitializeObjectAttributes function to initialize this structure. If the caller is not running in a system thread context, it must set the OBJ_KERNEL_HANDLE attribute when it calls InitializeObjectAttributes. This parameter is optional and can be NULL.

params.name: Uow
params.description: A pointer to a GUID that KTM uses as the new transaction object's unit of work (UOW) identifier. This parameter is optional and can be NULL. If this parameter is NULL, KTM generates a GUID and assigns it to the transaction object. For more information, see the following Remarks section.

params.name: TmHandle
params.description: A handle to a transaction manager object that was obtained by a previous call to ZwCreateTransactionManager or ZwOpenTransactionManager. KTM assigns the new transaction object to the specified transaction manager object. If this parameter is NULL, KTM assigns the new transaction object to a transaction manager later, when a resource manager creates an enlistment for the transaction.

params.name: CreateOptions
params.description: Optional object creation flags. The following table contains the available flags, which are defined in Ktmtypes.h.

params.name: IsolationLevel
params.description: Reserved for future use. Callers must set this parameter to zero.

params.name: IsolationFlags
params.description: Reserved for future use. Callers should set this parameter to zero.

params.name: Timeout
params.description: A pointer to a time-out value. If the transaction has not been committed by the time specified by this parameter, KTM rolls back the transaction. The time-out value is expressed in system time units (100-nanosecond intervals), and can specify either an absolute time or a relative time. If the value pointed to by Timeout is negative, the expiration time is relative to the current system time. Otherwise, the expiration time is absolute. This pointer is optional and can be NULL if you do not want the transaction to have a time-out value. If Timeout = NULL or Timeout* = 0, the transaction never times out. (You can also use ZwSetInformationTransaction to set a time-out value.)

params.name: Description
params.description: A pointer to a caller-supplied UNICODE_STRING structure that contains a NULL-terminated string. The string provides a description of the transaction. KTM stores a copy of the string and includes the string in messages that it writes to the log stream. The maximum string length is MAX_TRANSACTION_DESCRIPTION_LENGTH. This parameter is optional and can be NULL.

returns.description: ZwCreateTransaction returns STATUS_SUCCESS if the operation succeeds. Otherwise, this function might return one of the following values:

functions.name: NtCreateTransactionManager

params.name: DesiredAccess
params.description: An ACCESS_MASK value that specifies the caller's requested access to the transaction manager object. In addition to the access rights that are defined for all kinds of objects (see ACCESS_MASK), the caller can specify any of the following access right flags for transaction manager objects.

params.name: ObjectAttributes
params.description: A pointer to an OBJECT_ATTRIBUTES structure that specifies the object name and other attributes. Use the InitializeObjectAttributes function to initialize this structure. If the caller is not running in a system thread context, it must set the OBJ_KERNEL_HANDLE attribute when it calls InitializeObjectAttributes. This parameter is optional and can be NULL.

params.name: LogFileName
params.description: A pointer to a UNICODE_STRING structure that contains the path and file name of a CLFS log file stream to be associated with the transaction manager object. This parameter must be NULL if the CreateOptions parameter is TRANSACTION_MANAGER_VOLATILE. Otherwise, this parameter must be non-NULL. For more information, see the following Remarks section.

params.name: CreateOptions
params.description: Optional object creation flags. The following table contains the available flags, which are defined in Ktmtypes.h.

params.name: NotificationLength

params.description: A pointer to a value that specifies a relative or absolute time, in units of 100 nanoseconds. This pointer is optional and can be NULL.

params.name: AsynchronousContext

params.description: A pointer to a caller-allocated buffer that contains the input data for the operation. The format for the data in this buffer depends on the power control code specified by the PowerControlCode parameter. The InBuffer parameter is optional and can be specified as NULL if the specified operation requires no input data.

params.name: InBufferSize
params.description: The size, in bytes, of the input buffer that is pointed to by the InBuffer parameter. If InBuffer is NULL, set InBufferSize to zero.

params.name: OutBuffer
params.description: A pointer to a caller-allocated buffer that is to contain the output data from the operation. The format for the data in this buffer depends on the power control code specified by the PowerControlCode parameter. The OutBuffer parameter is optional and can be specified as NULL if the specified operation produces no output data.

params.name: OutBufferSize
params.description: The size, in bytes, of the output buffer that is pointed to by the OutBuffer parameter. If OutBuffer is NULL, set OutBufferSize to zero.

params.name: BytesReturned
params.description: A pointer to a location into which the function writes the number of bytes of data that were written to the buffer that is pointed to by OutBuffer. The number of bytes written will be less than or equal to OutBufferSize. This parameter is optional and can be specified as NULL if the caller does not need to know how many bytes were written to the output buffer.

returns.description: PoFxPowerControl returns STATUS_SUCCESS if the requested operation succeeds. Possible error return values include the following status code.

functions.name: PoFxPowerOnCrashdumpDevice
functions.summary: The PoFxPowerOnCrashdumpDevice function requests that a crash-dump device be turned on.

params.name: Handle
params.description: A handle that represents the registration of the crash-dump device with the Windows power management framework (PoFx). The device driver previously received this handle from the PoFxRegisterDevice function.

params.name: Context
params.description: A pointer to a device-specific context. This pointer is passed as an input parameter to the PowerOnDumpDeviceCallback callback function that is implemented by the platform extension plug-in (PEP) for the device. The context information is stored in a format that is defined by the device driver and is understood by the PEP. This context is opaque to the operating system. The driver can set this parameter to NULL if the PEP does not require a context.

returns.description: PoFxPowerOnCrashdumpDevice returns STATUS_SUCCESS if the function succeeds in turning on power to the device. Possible error return values include the following status codes.

functions.name: PoFxQueryCurrentComponentPerfState
functions.summary: The PoFxQueryCurrentComponentPerfState function retrieves the active performance state in a component's performance state set.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS PoFxQueryCurrentComponentPerfState(POHANDLE Handle, ULONG Flags, ULONG Component, ULONG SetIndex, PULONGLONG CurrentPerf);

params.name: Handle
params.description: A handle that represents the registration of the device with power management framework (PoFx). The device driver previously received this handle from the PoFxRegisterDevice function.

params.name: Flags
params.description: Set to 0. Currently, no flags are defined for this function.

params.name: Component
params.description: The index that identifies the component whose performance state is being retrieved. This parameter is an index into the Components array in the PO_FX_DEVICE structure that the device driver used to register the device with PoFx. If the Components array contains N elements, component indexes range from 0 to N, 1.

params.name: SetIndex
params.description: The index that identifies the performance state set whose performance is being queried. This parameter is an index into the PerfStateSets array in the PO_FX_COMPONENT_PERF_INFO structure that the device driver used to register the component performance states with PoFx. If the PerfStateSets array contains N elements, performance state set indexes range from 0 to N, 1.

params.name: CurrentPerf
params.description: A pointer to variable in which the current performance state for the specified performance state set is returned. For more information about the value that is returned, see Remarks.

returns.description: PoFxQueryCurrentComponentPerfState returns STATUS_SUCCESS if the requested operation succeeds. Possible error return values include the following status codes.

functions.name: PoFxRegisterComponentPerfStates
functions.summary: The PoFxRegisterComponentPerfStates function registers a device component for performance state management by the power management framework (PoFx).
functions.signature: NTSTATUS PoFxRegisterComponentPerfStates(POHANDLE Handle, ULONG Component, ULONGLONG Flags, PPO_FX_COMPONENT_PERF_STATE_CALLBACK ComponentPerfStateCallback, PPO_FX_COMPONENT_PERF_INFO InputStateInfo, PPO_FX_COMPONENT_PERF_INFO * OutputStateInfo);

params.name: Handle
params.description: A handle that represents the registration of the device with PoFx. The device driver previously received this handle from the PoFxRegisterDevice function.

params.name: Component
params.description: The index that identifies the component whose performance states will be managed. This parameter is an index into the Components array in the PO_FX_DEVICE structure that the device driver used to register the device with PoFx. If the Components array contains N elements, component indexes range from 0 to N, 1.

params.name: Flags
params.description: The flags that modify the behavior of the performance state registration. Set this member to zero or to one of the following flag PO_FX_FLAG_PERF_XXX bits:

params.name: ComponentPerfStateCallback
params.description: A pointer to a ComponentPerfStateCallback function. This function is called when PoFx has completed logging and notifying the PEP about a performance state transition that is initiated by the driver’s call to PoFxIssueComponentPerfStateChange or PoFxIssueComponentPerfStateChangeMultiple. This callback may be the same for all components and all devices; PoFx provides the device handle and component index in each completion call.

params.name: InputStateInfo
params.description: If the driver provides performance state info, this parameter contains a pointer to a driver allocated PO_FX_COMPONENT_PERF_INFO structure that provides performance state information to PoFx. If the driver requires performance state information from the PEP, this parameter must be set to NULL.

params.name: OutputStateInfo
params.description: If the driver requires performance state information from the PEP, after a successful registration this parameter contains a pointer to a PO_FX_COMPONENT_PERF_INFO structure that provides performance state information defined by the PEP. If the driver provides performance state info, this parameter must be set to NULL.

returns.description: PoFxRegisterComponentPerfStates returns STATUS_SUCCESS if PoFx accepts the device's registration of performance states. If any of the necessary information is not provided or incorrect, registration will fail with a return code other than STATUS_SUCCESS. Possible error return values include the following status codes.

functions.name: PoFxRegisterCrashdumpDevice
functions.summary: The PoFxRegisterCrashdumpDevice function registers a crash-dump device.

params.name: Handle
params.description: A handle that represents the registration of the crash-dump device with the Windows power management framework (PoFx). The device driver previously received this handle from the PoFxRegisterDevice function.

returns.description: PoFxRegisterCrashdumpDevice returns STATUS_SUCCESS if the function successfully registers the crash-dump device. Possible error return values include the following status codes.

functions.name: PoFxRegisterDevice
functions.summary: The PoFxRegisterDevice function registers a device with the power management framework (PoFx).
functions.signature: NTSTATUS PoFxRegisterDevice(PDEVICE_OBJECT Pdo, PPO_FX_DEVICE Device, POHANDLE * Handle);

params.name: Pdo
params.description: A pointer to a physical device object (PDO). This parameter points to a DEVICE_OBJECT structure that represents the physical device that is being registered. The caller is the power policy owner for the device, which is typically the device's function driver.

params.name: Device
params.description: A pointer to a caller-allocated PO_FX_DEVICE structure that contains the registration information for the device. This structure contains pointers to a set of callback functions that are implemented by the device driver. PoFx calls these functions to communicate with the driver.

params.name: Handle
params.description: A pointer to a location into which the function writes a handle that represents the registration of the device with PoFx. The device driver passes this handle as an input parameter to the other PoFxXxx functions that it calls. The driver must first call PoFxRegisterDevice to register the device before the driver calls any other PoFxXxx functions to power-manage the device.

returns.description: PoFxRegisterDevice returns STATUS_SUCCESS if the function successfully registers the device. Possible error return values include the following status codes.

functions.name: PoFxReportDevicePoweredOn
functions.summary: The PoFxReportDevicePoweredOn function notifies the power management framework (PoFx) that the device completed the requested transition to the D0 (fully on) power state.

params.name: Handle
params.description: A handle that represents the registration of the device with the power management framework (PoFx). The device driver previously received this handle from the PoFxRegisterDevice function.

returns.description: No value.

functions.name: PoFxSetComponentLatency
functions.summary: The PoFxSetComponentLatency function specifies the maximum latency that can be tolerated in the transition from the idle condition to the active condition in the specified component.
functions.signature: void PoFxSetComponentLatency(POHANDLE Handle, ULONG Component, ULONGLONG Latency);

params.name: Handle
params.description: A handle that represents the registration of the device with the power management framework (PoFx). The device driver previously received this handle from the PoFxRegisterDevice function.

params.name: Component
params.description: The index that identifies the component. This parameter is an index into the Components array in the PO_FX_DEVICE structure that the device driver used to register the device with PoFx. If the Components array contains N elements, component indexes range from 0 to N, 1.

params.name: Latency
params.description: The maximum latency, in 100-nanosecond units, that can be tolerated in the specified component. For more information, see Remarks.

returns.description: No value.

functions.name: PoFxSetComponentResidency
functions.summary: The PoFxSetComponentResidency function sets the estimated time for how long a component is likely to remain idle after the component enters the idle condition.
functions.signature: void PoFxSetComponentResidency(POHANDLE Handle, ULONG Component, ULONGLONG Residency);

params.name: Handle
params.description: A handle that represents the registration of the device with the power management framework (PoFx). The device driver previously received this handle from the PoFxRegisterDevice function.

params.name: Component
params.description: The index that identifies the component. This parameter is an index into the Components array in the PO_FX_DEVICE structure that the device driver used to register the device with PoFx. If the Components array contains N elements, component indexes range from 0 to N, 1.

params.name: Residency
params.description: The estimated residency time, in 100-nanosecond units. This parameter is a hint to PoFx about how long the component is likely to remain idle after a transition from the active condition to the idle condition. For more information, see Remarks.

returns.description: No value.

functions.name: PoFxSetComponentWake
functions.summary: The PoFxSetComponentWake function indicates whether the driver arms the specified component to wake whenever the component enters the idle condition.
functions.signature: void PoFxSetComponentWake(POHANDLE Handle, ULONG Component, BOOLEAN WakeHint);

params.name: Handle
params.description: A handle that represents the registration of the device with the power management framework (PoFx). The device driver previously received this handle from the PoFxRegisterDevice function.

params.name: Component
params.description: The index that identifies the component. This parameter is an index into the Components array in the PO_FX_DEVICE structure that the device driver used to register the device with PoFx. If the Components array contains N elements, component indexes range from 0 to N, 1.

params.name: WakeHint
params.description: Whether the driver arms the component to wake whenever the component enters the idle condition. If TRUE, the driver arms the component to wake. If FALSE, the driver does not arm the component to wake.

returns.description: No value.

functions.name: PoFxSetDeviceIdleTimeout
functions.summary: The PoFxSetDeviceIdleTimeout function specifies the minimum time interval from when the last component of the device enters the idle condition to when the power management framework (PoFx) calls the driver's DevicePowerNotRequiredCallback function.

params.name: Handle
params.description: A handle that represents the registration of the device with PoFx. The device driver previously received this handle from the PoFxRegisterDevice function.

params.name: IdleTimeout
params.description: The idle time-out interval in 100-nanosecond units. For more information, see Remarks.

returns.description: No value.

functions.name: PoFxSetTargetDripsDevicePowerState
functions.summary: This function is called to notify the power manager of the device's target device power state for DRIPS. The driver can override the DRIPS constraint provided by the PEP.

params.name: Handle
params.description: A handle that represents the registration of the device with PoFx. The device driver previously received this handle from the PoFxRegisterDevice function.

params.name: TargetState
params.description: Specifies the target DRIPS device power state. Possible values are defined in the DEVICE_POWER_STATE enumeration. This value must be lower than the existing device constraint. A device power state of PowerDeviceUnspecified resets to the PEP provided constraint.

returns.description: Returns STATUS_SUCCESS if the target state was accepted.

functions.name: PoFxStartDevicePowerManagement
functions.summary: The PoFxStartDevicePowerManagement function completes the registration of a device with the power management framework (PoFx) and starts device power management.

params.name: Handle
params.description: A handle that represents the registration of the device with the power management framework (PoFx). The device driver previously received this handle from the PoFxRegisterDevice function.

returns.description: No value.

functions.name: PoFxUnregisterDevice
functions.summary: The PoFxUnregisterDevice function removes the registration of a device from the power management framework (PoFx).

params.name: Handle
params.description: A handle that represents the registration of the device with PoFx. The device driver previously received this handle from the PoFxRegisterDevice function.

returns.description: No value.

functions.name: PoGetSystemWake
functions.summary: The PoGetSystemWake function determines whether a specified IRP has been marked as waking the system from a sleeping state.

params.name: Irp
params.description: A pointer to an IRP.

returns.description: PoGetSystemWake returns one of the following:

functions.name: PoQueryPowerLimitAttributes
functions.summary: This function queries the attributes of a power limit request object.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS PoQueryPowerLimitAttributes(PVOID PowerLimitRequest, ULONG BufferCount, PPOWER_LIMIT_ATTRIBUTES Buffer, PULONG AttributeCount);

params.name: PowerLimitRequest
params.description: A pointer to the power limit request object returned by PoCreatePowerLimitRequest.

params.name: BufferCount
params.description: Entries of the parameter *Buffer*.

params.name: Buffer
params.description: A pre-allocated buffer to save POWER_LIMIT_ATTRIBUTES of each power limit types of power limit domains.

params.name: AttributeCount
params.description: A pointer to save the number of attributes this platform supports. It should be the sum of power limit types of all domains.

returns.description: Returns an NTSTATUS value.

functions.name: PoQueryPowerLimitValue
functions.summary: This function queries the limit values of a power limit request object.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS PoQueryPowerLimitValue(PVOID PowerLimitRequest, ULONG ValueCount, PPOWER_LIMIT_VALUE Values);

params.name: PowerLimitRequest
params.description: A pointer to the power limit request object returned by PoCreatePowerLimitRequest.

params.name: ValueCount
params.description: Supplies the number of limit values to query.

params.name: Values
params.description: Supplies a pointer to the buffer that contains target limits and stores the readout.

returns.description: Returns an NTSTATUS value.

functions.name: PoQueryWatchdogTime
functions.summary: The PoQueryWatchdogTime function indicates whether the power manager has enabled a watchdog time-out counter for any power IRP that is currently assigned to the device stack.

params.name: Pdo
params.description: A pointer to a physical device object (PDO). This parameter points to a DEVICE_OBJECT structure that represents a physical device.

params.name: SecondsRemaining
params.description: A pointer to a location into which the function writes the time, in seconds, that remains before the next power watchdog time-out is set to occur.

returns.description: PoQueryWatchdogTime returns TRUE if a watchdog-enabled power IRP is currently assigned to the device stack. Otherwise, it returns FALSE.

functions.name: PoRegisterDeviceForIdleDetection
functions.summary: The PoRegisterDeviceForIdleDetection function enables or cancels idle detection and sets idle time-out values for a device.
functions.signature: PULONG PoRegisterDeviceForIdleDetection(PDEVICE_OBJECT DeviceObject, ULONG ConservationIdleTime, ULONG PerformanceIdleTime, DEVICE_POWER_STATE State);

params.name: DeviceObject
params.description: A pointer to the driver-created DEVICE_OBJECT for the device. On Windows 2000 and later systems, this parameter can point to a physical device object (PDO) or a functional device object (FDO). On Windows 98/Me, this parameter must point to the PDO of the underlying device.

params.name: ConservationIdleTime
params.description: Sets the time-out value (in seconds) to apply when the system power policy optimizes for energy conservation. Specify zero to disable idle detection when conservation policy is in effect.

params.name: PerformanceIdleTime
params.description: Sets the time-out value (in seconds) to apply when the system power policy optimizes for performance. Specify zero to disable idle detection when performance policy is in effect.

params.name: State
params.description: Specifies the device power state to be requested in an IRP_MN_SET_POWER request when either ConservationIdleTime or PerformanceIdleTime has been met. Possible values are the DEVICE_POWER_STATE values.

returns.description: PoRegisterDeviceForIdleDetection returns a pointer to the idle counter to indicate that idle detection has been enabled. It returns NULL to indicate that idle detection has been disabled, that an idle counter could not be allocated, or that one or both of the time-out values were invalid.

functions.name: PoRegisterForEffectivePowerModeNotifications
functions.summary: The PoRegisterForEffectivePowerModeNotifications function registers a callback to receive effective power mode change notifications.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS PoRegisterForEffectivePowerModeNotifications(ULONG Version, PPO_EFFECTIVE_POWER_MODE_CALLBACK Callback, PVOID Context, PO_EPM_HANDLE * RegistrationHandle, PDEVICE_OBJECT DeviceObject);

params.name: Version
params.description: Supplies the maximum effective power mode version the caller understands. If the effective power mode comes from a later version, it is mapped to a compatible version that is then passed to the callback.

params.name: Callback
params.description: A pointer to the callback to call when the effective power mode changes. This will also be called once upon registration to supply the current mode. If multiple callbacks are registered, those callbacks can be called concurrently.

params.name: Context
params.description: Caller-specified opaque context.

params.name: RegistrationHandle
params.description: This is a pointer to a variable that receives a handle to the registration. This handle can be used to unregister the callback function.

params.name: DeviceObject
params.description: This is an optional parameter that, if specified, provides a registered callback (such as from a driver) with the specified device context.

returns.description: Returns S_OK (zero) if the call was successful, and a nonzero value if the call failed.

functions.name: PoRegisterPowerSettingCallback
functions.summary: The PoRegisterPowerSettingCallback function registers a power-setting callback function to receive notifications of changes in the specified power setting.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS PoRegisterPowerSettingCallback(PDEVICE_OBJECT DeviceObject, LPCGUID SettingGuid, PPOWER_SETTING_CALLBACK Callback, PVOID Context, PVOID * Handle);

params.name: DeviceObject
params.description: A pointer to a DEVICE_OBJECT structure that is associated with the caller of this function. This parameter is optional. It is used internally only for debugging purposes. If this parameter is not supplied, it must be set to NULL.

params.name: SettingGuid
params.description: A pointer to the GUID that represents the power setting for this registration. When the specified power setting changes, the power manager calls the callback function to notify the driver of the change and to supply the new value of the setting. For more information, see Remarks.

params.name: Callback
params.description: A pointer to a caller-implemented power-setting callback function that the power manager calls when the specified power setting changes. For the functional prototype for the callback function, see Power-Setting Callback.

params.name: Context
params.description: A pointer to the context for the callback function. This parameter is optional. It is provided so that a driver or device context can be passed to the callback function. If this parameter is not used, it must be set to NULL.

params.name: Handle
params.description: A handle that the power manager uses to represent the callback function. A driver must subsequently supply this handle in a call to PoUnregisterPowerSettingCallback to unregister the callback function.

returns.description: PoRegisterPowerSettingCallback returns one of the following:

functions.name: PoRegisterSystemState
functions.summary: The PoRegisterSystemState function registers the system as busy due to certain activity.

params.name: StateHandle
params.description: A pointer to a caller-supplied buffer for a registration state handle. The size, in bytes, of the buffer is sizeof(ULONG). If NULL, this is a new registration. If non-NULL, this parameter points to a handle that was returned by a previous call to PoRegisterSystemState.

params.name: Flags
params.description: Indicates the type of activity, as specified by a bitwise OR of one or more of the following values:

returns.description: PoRegisterSystemState returns a handle to be used later to change or unregister the system busy state. It returns NULL if the handle could not be allocated.

functions.name: PoRequestPowerIrp
functions.summary: The PoRequestPowerIrp function allocates a power IRP and sends it to the top driver in the device stack for the specified device.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS PoRequestPowerIrp(PDEVICE_OBJECT DeviceObject, UCHAR MinorFunction, POWER_STATE PowerState, PREQUEST_POWER_COMPLETE CompletionFunction, PVOID Context, PIRP * Irp);

params.name: DeviceObject
params.description: A pointer to the target DEVICE_OBJECT for the IRP. In Windows 2000 and later versions of Windows, this parameter can point to a physical device object (PDO) or a functional device object (FDO). In Windows 98/Me, this parameter must point to the PDO of the underlying device.

params.name: MinorFunction
params.description: Specifies one of the following minor power IRP codes: IRP_MN_QUERY_POWER, IRP_MN_SET_POWER, or IRP_MN_WAIT_WAKE.

params.name: PowerState
params.description: Specifies a POWER_STATE value to pass in the IRP. For IRP_MN_SET_POWER and IRP_MN_QUERY_POWER, specify the requested new device power state. Possible values are DEVICE_POWER_STATE values.

params.name: CompletionFunction
params.description: A pointer to the caller's PowerCompletion callback function. The I/O manager calls this function when the IRP has completed. This parameter is optional and can be set to NULL if no PowerCompletion callback function is needed.

params.name: Context
params.description: A pointer to a caller-supplied context to be passed through to the PowerCompletion callback. When the caller requests a device set-power IRP in response to a system set-power IRP, Context should contain the system set-power IRP that triggered the request.

params.name: Irp
params.description: A pointer to a caller-supplied variable in which PoRequestPowerIrp returns a pointer to the IRP that it allocates. Specify a value for Irp only if the MinorFunction parameter is set to IRP_MN_WAIT_WAKE. Otherwise, this parameter should always be NULL because the IRP might be completed before PoRequestPowerIrp returns, causing this parameter to point to memory that has already been discarded.

returns.description: PoRequestPowerIrp returns one of the following:

functions.name: PoSetDeviceBusyEx
functions.summary: The PoSetDeviceBusyEx function notifies the power manager that the device associated with the specified idle counter is busy.

params.name: IdlePointer
params.description: A pointer to an idle counter. This is a pointer value that was previously returned by the PoRegisterDeviceForIdleDetection function. Because PoRegisterDeviceForIdleDetection might return a NULL pointer, the caller must verify that the pointer is non-NULL before it calls PoSetDeviceBusyEx.

returns.description: No value.

functions.name: PoSetPowerLimitValue
functions.summary: This function sets power limit values.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS PoSetPowerLimitValue(PVOID PowerLimitRequest, PCOUNTED_REASON_CONTEXT Reason, ULONG ValueCount, PPOWER_LIMIT_VALUE Values);

params.name: PowerLimitRequest
params.description: A pointer to the power limit request object returned by PoCreatePowerLimitRequest.

params.name: Reason
params.description: A pointer to a COUNTED_REASON_CONTEXT structure that describes why the caller is making this power limit update.

params.name: ValueCount
params.description: Supplies the number of limit values to be updated.

params.name: Values
params.description: Supplies a pointer to the buffer that contains target limits and stores the readout.

returns.description: Returns an NTSTATUS value.

functions.name: PoSetPowerRequest
functions.summary: The PoSetPowerRequest function increments the count for the specified power request type.

params.name: PowerRequest
params.description: A pointer to a power request object that was created by the PoCreatePowerRequest function.

params.name: Type
params.description: The type of power request. Set this parameter to the following POWER_REQUEST_TYPE enumeration value:

returns.description: PoSetPowerRequest returns STATUS_SUCCESS if the call is successful. If the call fails, possible error return codes include the following:

functions.name: PoSetPowerState
functions.summary: The PoSetPowerState function notifies the system of a change in the device power state for a device.
functions.signature: POWER_STATE PoSetPowerState(PDEVICE_OBJECT DeviceObject, POWER_STATE_TYPE Type, POWER_STATE State);

params.name: DeviceObject
params.description: A pointer to the target DEVICE_OBJECT.

params.name: Type
params.description: Indicates a POWER_STATE_TYPE value. Drivers must specify DevicePowerState.

params.name: State
params.description: Specifies the power state to be set. Drivers must specify a DEVICE_POWER_STATE value.

returns.description: On Windows 2000 and later versions of the operating system, PoSetPowerState returns the previous power state. On Windows 98/Me, PoSetPowerState returns the state passed in State.

functions.name: PoSetSystemState
functions.summary: Drivers call the PoSetSystemState function to indicate that the system is active.

params.name: Flags
params.description: Indicates the system activity, as specified by a bitwise OR of one or more of the following values:

returns.description: No value.

functions.name: PoSetSystemWake
functions.summary: The PoSetSystemWake function marks the specified IRP as one that contributed to waking the system from a sleep state.

params.name: Irp
params.description: A pointer to the wait/wake IRP.

returns.description: No value.

functions.name: PoSetSystemWakeDevice
functions.summary: The PoSetSystemWakeDevice function attempts to extract a PDO from the supplied device object. If a valid PDO is found then it is added to the list of sources which contributed to waking the system from a sleep state. There is a time interval (currently 2 seconds) during which, from the completed wait/wake IRPs, the power manager attempts to build a list of system wake sources.

params.name: DeviceObject
params.description: Supplies a pointer to the device object that has wait/wake IRPs contributing to waking the system from a sleep state.

returns.description: No value.

functions.name: PoStartDeviceBusy
functions.summary: The PoStartDeviceBusy function marks the start of a period of time in which the device is busy.

params.name: IdlePointer
params.description: A pointer to an idle counter. This is a pointer value that was previously returned by the PoRegisterDeviceForIdleDetection function. Because PoRegisterDeviceForIdleDetection might return a NULL pointer, the caller must verify that the pointer is non-NULL before it calls PoStartDeviceBusy.

returns.description: No value.

functions.name: PoStartNextPowerIrp
functions.summary: The PoStartNextPowerIrp function signals the power manager that the driver is ready to handle the next power IRP. (Windows Server 2003, Windows XP, and Windows 2000 only.)

params.name: Irp
params.description: A pointer to an IRP in which the major function code is IRP_MJ_POWER.

returns.description: No value.

functions.name: PoUnregisterFromEffectivePowerModeNotifications
functions.summary: The PoUnregisterFromEffectivePowerModeNotifications function unregisters from effective power mode change notifications. This function is intended to be called from cleanup code and will wait for all callbacks to complete before unregistering.

params.name: RegistrationHandle
params.description: The handle corresponding to a single power mode registration. This handle should have been saved by the caller after the call to PowerRegisterForEffectivePowerModeNotifications and passed in here.

returns.description: Returns S_OK (zero) if the call was successful, and a nonzero value if the call failed.

functions.name: PoUnregisterPowerSettingCallback
functions.summary: The PoUnregisterPowerSettingCallback function unregisters a power-setting callback function that a driver previously registered by calling the PoRegisterPowerSettingCallback function.

params.name: Handle
params.description: A handle to a callback function that a driver registered by calling PoRegisterPowerSettingCallback.

returns.description: PoUnregisterPowerSettingCallback returns one of the following:

functions.name: PoUnregisterSystemState
functions.summary: The PoUnregisterSystemState function cancels a system state registration created by PoRegisterSystemState.

params.name: StateHandle
params.description: A pointer to a handle previously returned by PoRegisterSystemState.

returns.description: No value.

functions.name: PopEntryList
functions.summary: The PopEntryList function removes the first entry from a singly linked list of SINGLE_LIST_ENTRY structures.

params.name: ListHead
params.description: Pointer to the SINGLE_LIST_ENTRY structure that represents the head of the list. On return, ListHead->Next points to the beginning of the list with the first entry removed.

returns.description: PopEntryList returns a pointer to the entry removed from the list, or NULL if the list is currently empty.

functions.name: ProbeForRead
functions.summary: The ProbeForRead function checks that a user-mode buffer actually resides in the user portion of the address space, and is correctly aligned.
functions.signature: void ProbeForRead(volatile void * Address, SIZE_T Length, ULONG Alignment);

params.name: Address
params.description: Specifies the beginning of the user-mode buffer.

params.name: Length
params.description: Specifies the length, in bytes, of the user-mode buffer.

params.name: Alignment
params.description: Specifies the required alignment, in bytes, of the beginning of the user-mode buffer.

returns.description: No value.

functions.name: ProbeForWrite
functions.summary: > [!WARNING] > The ProbeForWrite function is not recommended for use in current software, and is included for historical compatibility only. Use ProbeForRead instead when validating user buffers. See Remarks for more info.
functions.signature: void ProbeForWrite(volatile void * Address, SIZE_T Length, ULONG Alignment);

params.name: Address
params.description: Specifies the beginning of the user-mode buffer.

params.name: Length
params.description: Specifies the length, in bytes, of the user-mode buffer. See additional information in the Remarks section.

params.name: Alignment

functions.name: RtlFindClearBits

params.name: NumberToFind
params.description: Specifies how many contiguous clear bits will satisfy this request.

params.name: HintIndex
params.description: Specifies a zero-based bit position from which to start looking for a clear bit range of the given size.

returns.description: RtlFindClearBits either returns the zero-based starting bit index for a clear bit range of at least the requested size, or it returns 0xFFFFFFFF if it cannot find such a range within the given bitmap.

functions.name: RtlFindClearBitsAndSet

params.name: BitMapHeader
params.description: A pointer to the RTL_BITMAP structure that describes the bitmap. This structure must have been initialized by the RtlInitializeBitMap function.

params.name: HintIndex
params.description: Specifies a zero-based bit position from which to start looking for a clear bit range of the given size.

returns.description: RtlFindClearBitsAndSet either returns the zero-based starting bit index for a clear bit range of the requested size that it set, or it returns 0xFFFFFFFF if it cannot find such a range within the given bitmap variable.

functions.name: RtlFindClearRuns

params.name: BitMapHeader

params.name: RunArray
params.description: Pointer to the first element in a caller-allocated array for the bit position and length of each clear run found in the given bitmap variable.

params.description: Specifies the maximum number of clear runs to satisfy this request.

params.description: If TRUE, specifies that the function is to search the entire bitmap for the longest clear runs it can find. Otherwise, the function stops searching when it has found the number of clear runs specified by SizeOfRunArray.

returns.description: RtlFindClearRuns returns the number of clear runs found.

functions.name: RtlFindFirstRunClear

params.description: A pointer to the RTL_BITMAP structure that describes the bitmap. This structure must have been initialized by the RtlInitializeBitMap function.

params.name: StartingIndex
params.description: Pointer to a variable in which the starting index of the initial clear run in the bitmap is returned. This is a zero-based value indicating the bit position of the first clear bit in the returned range. Its value is meaningless if RtlFindFirstRunClear cannot find a run of clear bits.

returns.description: RtlFindFirstRunClear returns either the number of bits in the run beginning at StartingIndex, or zero if it cannot find a run of clear bits within the bitmap.

functions.name: RtlFindLastBackwardRunClear

params.name: BitMapHeader
params.description: A pointer to the RTL_BITMAP structure that describes the bitmap. This structure must have been initialized by the RtlInitializeBitMap function.

params.name: StartingRunIndex
params.description: Pointer to a variable in which the starting index of the clear run found in the bitmap is returned. This is a zero-based value indicating the bit position of the first clear bit in the run preceding the given FromIndex. Its value is meaningless if RtlFindLastBackwardRunClear cannot find a run of clear bits.

returns.description: RtlFindLastBackwardRunClear returns the number of bits in the run beginning at StartingRunIndex, or zero if it cannot find a run of clear bits preceding FromIndex in the bitmap.

functions.name: RtlSetDaclSecurityDescriptor
functions.summary: The RtlSetDaclSecurityDescriptor function sets the DACL information of an absolute-format security descriptor, or if there is already a DACL present in the security descriptor, it is superseded.

params.name: SecurityDescriptor
params.description: A pointer to a SECURITY_DESCRIPTOR structure. This structure is the security descriptor to which the DACL is to be applied.

params.name: DaclPresent
params.description: Whether to indicate that a DACL is present in the security descriptor. If this parameter is FALSE, RtlSetDaclSecurityDescriptor sets the SE_DACL_PRESENT control flag in the security descriptor to FALSE. In this case, the remaining optional parameters (Dacl and DaclDefaulted) are ignored. If DaclPresent is TRUE, the SE_DACL_PRESENT flag in the security descriptor is set to TRUE and the remaining optional parameters are not ignored. For more information about the SE_DACL_PRESENT flag, see SECURITY_DESCRIPTOR_CONTROL.

params.name: Dacl
params.description: A pointer to the DACL for the security descriptor. If this parameter is NULL, the DACL pointer in the security descriptor is set to NULL. A NULL DACL pointer unconditionally grants all access to an object and is not the same as an empty DACL. An empty DACL denies all access to an object. If Dacl is non-NULL, the ACL structure supplied by the caller is referenced by, but not copied into, the security descriptor. The caller can allocate the ACL structure from paged system memory, and can call the RtlCreateAcl function to initialize the structure.

params.name: DaclDefaulted
params.description: Whether the DACL was supplied by some default mechanism, or was explicitly specified by the caller. If this parameter is TRUE, the DACL was supplied by a default mechanism. If DaclDefaulted is FALSE, the caller explicitly specified the DACL. RtlSetDaclSecurityDescriptor copies the value specified for this parameter to the SE_DACL_DEFAULTED control flag in the security descriptor. For more information about the SE_DACL_DEFAULTED flag, see SECURITY_DESCRIPTOR_CONTROL.

returns.description: RtlSetDaclSecurityDescriptor can return one of the following status values.

functions.summary: SeAccessCheck determines whether the requested access rights can be granted to an object protected by a security descriptor and an object owner.

params.name: SecurityDescriptor
params.description: Pointer to the SECURITY_DESCRIPTOR structure that describes the security descriptor protecting the object being accessed.

params.name: SubjectSecurityContext
params.description: Pointer to the opaque SECURITY_SUBJECT_CONTEXT structure that specifies the subject's captured security context.

params.name: SubjectContextLocked
params.description: Boolean value that indicates whether the user's subject context is locked, so that it does not have to be locked again.

params.name: DesiredAccess
params.description: Specifies the ACCESS_MASK bitmask for the access rights that the caller is attempting to acquire. If the caller sets the MAXIMUM_ALLOWED bit, the function performs all DACL checks. However, SeAccessCheck does not do any privilege checks unless the caller specifically requests them by setting the ACCESS_SYSTEM_SECURITY or WRITE_OWNER bits.

params.name: PreviouslyGrantedAccess
params.description: Specifies the ACCESS_MASK bitmask of access rights already granted, such as access rights granted as a result of holding a privilege.

params.name: Privileges
params.description: Pointer to a caller-supplied variable to be set to the address of the PRIVILEGE_SET structure that will be used as part of the access validation, or this parameter can be NULL. The returned buffer, if any, must be released by the caller with SeFreePrivileges.

params.name: GenericMapping
params.description: Pointer to the GENERIC_MAPPING structure associated with this object type. This value specifies the specific access rights implied by each GENERIC_*XXX* access right.

params.name: AccessMode
params.description: Specifies the access mode to be used in the check, either UserMode or KernelMode.

params.name: GrantedAccess
params.description: Pointer to a returned access mask indicating the granted access. If the caller specifies MAXIMUM_ALLOWED, and the DACL in SecurityDescriptor is NULL, then the function returns GENERIC_ALL plus any additional access the caller explicitly requests.

params.name: AccessStatus
params.description: Pointer to the status value indicating why access was denied.

returns.description: If access is allowed, SeAccessCheck returns TRUE.

params.name: FileAttributes
params.description: Specifies one or more FILE_ATTRIBUTE_*XXX* flags, which represent the file attributes to set if you create or overwrite a file. The caller usually specifies FILE_ATTRIBUTE_NORMAL, which sets the default attributes. For a list of valid FILE_ATTRIBUTE_*XXX* flags, see the CreateFile function. If no file is created or overwritten, *FileAttributes* is ignored.

params.name: ShareAccess
params.description: Type of share access, which is specified as zero or any combination of the following flags.

params.name: CreateDisposition
params.description: Specifies the action to perform if the file does or does not exist. *CreateDisposition* can be one of the values in the following table.

params.name: CreateOptions
params.description: Specifies the options to apply when the driver creates or opens the file. Use one or more of the flags in the following table.

params.name: EaBuffer
params.description: For device and intermediate drivers, this parameter must be a NULL pointer.

params.name: EaLength
params.description: For device and intermediate drivers, this parameter must be zero.

functions.name: ZwCreateSection
functions.summary: The ZwCreateSection function creates a section object.

params.name: SectionHandle
params.description: Pointer to a HANDLE variable that receives a handle to the section object.

params.name: DesiredAccess
params.description: Specifies an ACCESS_MASK value that determines the requested access to the object. In addition to the access rights that are defined for all types of objects (see ACCESS_MASK), the caller can specify any of the following access rights, which are specific to section objects:

params.name: ObjectAttributes
params.description: Pointer to an OBJECT_ATTRIBUTES structure that specifies the object name and other attributes. Use InitializeObjectAttributes to initialize this structure. If the caller is not running in a system thread context, it must set the OBJ_KERNEL_HANDLE attribute when it calls InitializeObjectAttributes.

params.name: MaximumSize
params.description: Specifies the maximum size, in bytes, of the section. ZwCreateSection rounds this value up to the nearest multiple of PAGE_SIZE. If the section is backed by the paging file, *MaximumSize* specifies the actual size of the section. If the section is backed by an ordinary file, *MaximumSize* specifies the maximum size that the file can be extended or mapped to.

params.name: SectionPageProtection
params.description: Specifies the protection to place on each page in the section. Use one of the following four values: PAGE_READONLY, PAGE_READWRITE, PAGE_EXECUTE, or PAGE_WRITECOPY. For a description of these values, see CreateFileMapping.

params.name: AllocationAttributes
params.description: Specifies a bitmask of SEC_*XXX* flags that determines the allocation attributes of the section. For a description of these flags, see CreateFileMapping.

params.name: FileHandle
params.description: Optionally specifies a handle for an open file object. If the value of *FileHandle* is NULL, the section is backed by the paging file. Otherwise, the section is backed by the specified file.

functions.name: ZwCreateTransaction
functions.summary: The ZwCreateTransaction function creates a transaction object.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS ZwCreateTransaction(PHANDLE TransactionHandle, ACCESS_MASK DesiredAccess, POBJECT_ATTRIBUTES ObjectAttributes, LPGUID Uow, HANDLE TmHandle, ULONG CreateOptions, ULONG IsolationLevel, ULONG IsolationFlags, PLARGE_INTEGER Timeout, PUNICODE_STRING Description);

params.name: TransactionHandle
params.description: A pointer to a caller-allocated variable that receives a handle to the new transaction object, if the call to ZwCreateTransaction succeeds.

params.name: DesiredAccess
params.description: An ACCESS_MASK value that specifies the caller's requested access to the transaction object. In addition to the access rights that are defined for all kinds of objects (see ACCESS_MASK), the caller can specify any of the following flags for transaction objects.

params.name: ObjectAttributes
params.description: A pointer to an OBJECT_ATTRIBUTES structure that specifies the object name and other attributes. Use the InitializeObjectAttributes function to initialize this structure. If the caller is not running in a system thread context, it must set the OBJ_KERNEL_HANDLE attribute when it calls InitializeObjectAttributes. This parameter is optional and can be NULL.

params.name: Uow
params.description: A pointer to a GUID that KTM uses as the new transaction object's unit of work (UOW) identifier. This parameter is optional and can be NULL. If this parameter is NULL, KTM generates a GUID and assigns it to the transaction object. For more information, see the following Remarks section.

params.name: TmHandle
params.description: A handle to a transaction manager object that was obtained by a previous call to ZwCreateTransactionManager or ZwOpenTransactionManager. KTM assigns the new transaction object to the specified transaction manager object. If this parameter is NULL, KTM assigns the new transaction object to a transaction manager later, when a resource manager creates an enlistment for the transaction.

params.name: CreateOptions
params.description: Optional object creation flags. The following table contains the available flags, which are defined in Ktmtypes.h.

params.name: IsolationLevel
params.description: Reserved for future use. Callers must set this parameter to zero.

params.name: IsolationFlags
params.description: Reserved for future use. Callers should set this parameter to zero.

params.name: Timeout
params.description: A pointer to a time-out value. If the transaction has not been committed by the time specified by this parameter, KTM rolls back the transaction. The time-out value is expressed in system time units (100-nanosecond intervals), and can specify either an absolute time or a relative time. If the value pointed to by Timeout is negative, the expiration time is relative to the current system time. Otherwise, the expiration time is absolute. This pointer is optional and can be NULL if you do not want the transaction to have a time-out value. If Timeout = NULL or Timeout* = 0, the transaction never times out. (You can also use ZwSetInformationTransaction to set a time-out value.)

params.name: Description
params.description: A pointer to a caller-supplied UNICODE_STRING structure that contains a NULL-terminated string. The string provides a description of the transaction. KTM stores a copy of the string and includes the string in messages that it writes to the log stream. The maximum string length is MAX_TRANSACTION_DESCRIPTION_LENGTH. This parameter is optional and can be NULL.

returns.description: ZwCreateTransaction returns STATUS_SUCCESS if the operation succeeds. Otherwise, this function might return one of the following values:
